description:
This is a pre-engagement or self-assessment checklist. It is not a gap analysis. Status per item: Not Started / In Progress / Implemented / Not Applicable, plus comments.

| Area | Items |
|---|---|
| AMLR awareness and strategic planning | AMLR knowledge at executive level; dedicated implementation owner or team; budget; timeline; gap analysis conducted; regulatory updates monitored |
| Governance and policy framework | Designated AML officer at appropriate seniority; board-level oversight; AML policy aligned with the AMLR; documented risk-based approach; enterprise-wide risk assessment; group-wide policies; regular independent compliance testing |
| Customer due diligence | Digital identity verification; risk-based CDD/EDD procedures; beneficial ownership verification; PEP screening and monitoring; source of funds and wealth for high-risk customers; ongoing and event-driven CDD and customer risk reassessment; onboarding aligned with AMLR standards |
| Transaction monitoring and reporting | Automated monitoring; behavioural analytics; scenarios tailored to the business model; real-time or near-real-time monitoring; cash transaction monitoring; cross-channel monitoring; suspicious activity reporting process and documentation; readiness for standardised reporting formats |
| Data management and technology | Customer data model; data quality framework; AML data governance; record retention; data protection compliance for AML processing; connectivity to external data sources; integration with beneficial ownership registers |
| Crypto-asset specifics (if applicable) | CDD at the lower threshold; travel rule; blockchain analytics; self-hosted wallet risk; crypto-specific risk assessment; EDD for cross-border crypto |
| Resources and training | Compliance staffing; AMLR training; technology expertise; budget; external expertise identified; change management plan |

canonical_name: Gap analysis (gap log and gap report) blueprint — Rating scales for gap analyses — 1. Standard 5-level deficiency scale
description:
| Level | Log value (EN) | Report label (EN) | Swedish | Descriptor | Recommended timing | House priority | Colour, if used |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Critical gaps | Critical deficiencies | Kritiska brister | One or more serious deficiencies that expose the company to an unacceptable level of risk. Could quickly result in extensive sanctions. | Immediate action | Immediate; board attention | Red |
| 4 | Extensive gaps | Extensive deficiencies | Omfattande brister | One or more significant deficiencies that, if not remedied, cause an undesirable level of risk. May result in significant sanctions. | As soon as possible | Within about 3 months | Orange |
| 3 | Significant gaps | Significant deficiencies | Betydande brister | Deficiencies that, if not remedied, mean an increased level of risk. May to some extent result in sanctions. | Within a reasonable time | Within 6–12 months | Yellow |
| 2 | Minor gaps | Minor deficiencies | Mindre brister | Only minor deficiencies. Improvement recommendations may be given. Not expected to result in sanctions. | At the next document update | Improvement | Light green |
| 1 | No gaps (Compliant) | No deficiencies | Inga brister | No apparent deficiencies identified. Improvement recommendations may still be given. | — | — | Green |

Supplementary values:

| Value | Swedish | Use |
|---|---|---|
| N/A | Ej tillämpligt | The provision does not apply. A reason is required. |
| Cannot be assessed | Kan inte bedömas | Evidence not obtained. State what is needed. Never default to "No gaps". |

**Basis for rating.** Three factors decide the level:
1. the level of risk the deficiency exposes the company to;
2. the sanction risk if the supervisor examines the area, informed by published sanction decisions and statements;

canonical_name: Gap analysis (gap log and gap report) blueprint — Thematic control points (quick scan and review checklist) — Typical cross-cutting findings to test for
description:
These are taken from the team's gap work.

- Governing documents state *what* but not *how*: who does it, when, how it is documented, and with which system support.
- Dependency on a key person for investigation and reporting, with no deputy procedure.
- No documented method for the BWRA. Typologies (*modus*) not described. Sources not cited. Inherent and residual risk missing for some risk areas.
- Controls credited in the BWRA without evidence that they are applied and work.
- No written reporting to the CEO and board; minutes too brief for an outsider to follow.
- No red thread from alert through investigation and EDD to the decision to report or not; the closing rationale is not documented.
- CDD and risk classification repeated at every transaction instead of risk-based updating; no next-review date.
- Customer risk classification not linked to the BWRA, monitoring or the collection of KYC information.
- Training limited to generic e-learning, not adapted to roles, or not documented.

description: The finding scale is the team's own (`gap-analysis/references/rating-scales.md`). Everything else in this file is a proposal `[TEAM INPUT]`.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Review scales, sampling and workbook layout — 1. Finding rating: the team's 5-level scale
description:
| Level | Label (*Swedish*) | Descriptor (short) | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Critical deficiencies (*Kritiska brister*) | Unacceptable risk level; could quickly result in extensive sanctions | Immediate |
| 4 | Extensive deficiencies (*Omfattande brister*) | Undesirable risk level if not remedied; may result in significant sanctions | Within about 3 months |
| 3 | Significant deficiencies (*Betydande brister*) | Increased risk level if not remedied; may to some extent result in sanctions | Within 6–12 months |
| 2 | Minor deficiencies (*Mindre brister*) | Improvements only; not expected to result in sanctions | Improvement |
| 1 | No deficiencies (*Inga brister*) | No apparent deficiencies | — |

**Basis for each rating:** risk level, sanction exposure (informed by published supervisory decisions) and process importance. The rating is a forecast.

**Pervasiveness adjusts the rating within the scale.** An exception in one item may be minor. The same exception across most of the items in a key control may be extensive.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Review scales, sampling and workbook layout — 2. Overall conclusion per area (proposal)
description:
| Conclusion | Swedish | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Effective | *Ändamålsenlig* | Only minor deficiencies or none |
| Largely effective | *I huvudsak ändamålsenlig* | Highest finding Significant |
| Partially effective | *Delvis ändamålsenlig* | At least one Extensive finding |
| Not effective | *Inte ändamålsenlig* | At least one Critical finding, or several Extensive findings in the same key control |

Judgement may lower a conclusion by one level, with a stated reason. It never raises one.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Review scales, sampling and workbook layout — 3. Key control assessment (proposal)
description:
| Dimension | Values |
|---|---|
| Design | Adequate / Partly adequate / Inadequate |
| Operating effectiveness | Effective / Effective with exceptions / Not effective / Not tested |
| Deficiency type (per finding) | Design / Operation / Documentation |

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Review scales, sampling and workbook layout — 4. Sampling guide (proposal)
description:
| Review type | Sample per key control or category | What it supports |
|---|---|---|
| Targeted check (the team's practice in operational review steps) | 5 latest or highest-risk items | Indicative findings; "x of 5" |
| Standard review | Risk-based and random mix, scaled to the population size and risk `[TEAM INPUT: house sample sizes]` | Findings with a stated frequency in the sample |
| Data analysis | Full population | Rates and trends (e.g. overdue reviews, alert ageing) |

**Rules**
- Define the population (source, period, filters) before selecting the sample, and record how the selection was made.
- Use targeted selection for known weak spots and random selection for coverage, and do not mix them in one rate.
- Replace an item only if it is out of scope, never because it is hard to test, and document the replacement.
- Report "x of n". Do not extrapolate from targeted or small samples.
- "Evidence not provided" counts as an exception.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Review scales, sampling and workbook layout — 5. Test workbook layout (Excel)
description:
| Sheet | Content |
|---|---|
| Instructions | Purpose, scope, criteria, period, colour legend, version log |
| Review plan | Area | Key control | Criteria | Test procedure | Population | Sample size | Selection method | Owner (client role) | Status |
| Populations | One block per population: source system, extraction date, period, filters, count |
| Test sheets (one per area) | Test-ID | Item ID (pseudonymised) | Attribute 1 … n (Pass / Exception / N/A) | Evidence reference | Comment | Exception → Finding ID |
| Findings log | ID | Area | Requirement / criterion | Criteria source | Observation | Evidence reference | Deficiency type | Root cause | Assessment | Rating | Recommendation | Priority / timing | Owner | Management response | Status |
| Scale | The 5-level scale, the overall conclusion rule, the test values |
| Lists | Dropdown values |
| Summary | Findings by area × rating; overall conclusion per area; exception counts per test |

**IDs:** findings R-[area]-[nn] (e.g. R-CDD-03); tests T-[area]-[nn]; sampled items with an area prefix (e.g. KYC-07, ALR-12). Keep the mapping from item ID to customer only in the restricted workpapers.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — Introduction
description:
This is a proposed programme `[TEAM INPUT]`. It is built from the AML/CTF requirements, the team's gap logs and thematic control points (`gap-analysis/references/thematic-control-points.md`) and the team's operational review step. Choose the areas from the review plan. For each area, record in the test sheet: Test-ID | Item ID (pseudonymised) | Attribute 1…n (Pass / Exception / N/A) | Evidence reference | Comment.

Swedish references are as used in the team's material. Verify them, and add AMLR articles for reviews close to its application date (`gap-analysis/references/amlr-national-mapping.md`).

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 1. Governance, reporting and internal control
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 6 kap. 1–2 §§; FFFS 2017:11 6 kap. 2–13 §§; the client's policy and internal control instruction.

**Evidence and populations**
- Appointment decisions and role descriptions for the designated member of management, the compliance officer and the independent audit function.
- The internal control and compliance monitoring plan and its results.
- Reports to the CEO and board for the period.
- Minutes of monitoring and review meetings with their supporting material (team model: the two latest).
- Internal audit reports and the follow-up list.

**Design**
- Are roles, responsibilities and independence documented?
- Does the plan say which key controls are tested, by whom, how often, and how results are reported?
- Are the proportionality decisions documented?

**Operating tests**
- Planned controls performed and documented (sample of plan items).
- Reports to the CEO and board delivered as described in the policy, with substance on CDD, monitoring and reporting.
- Minutes allow an outsider to follow what was presented and decided.
- Actions from earlier findings followed up.

**Typical findings:** no written reporting; minutes too brief; internal control limited to "attending meetings"; no testing of key controls; the compliance function is not independent of the areas it monitors.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 2. Business-wide risk assessment (as an input to the review)
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 2 kap. 1–2 §§; FFFS 2017:11 2 kap. 1 §.

**Evidence:** the BWRA, its method, the approval minutes, the evaluation record.

**Tests**
- Approved at the right level, and evaluated at least annually and before new products.
- Typologies (*modus*) described, with sources.
- Inherent and residual risk for all risk areas.
- Controls credited only where there is evidence they work.
- Conclusions used in customer risk classification, monitoring and training.

Use `aml-ctf-risk-assessment` for a full quality review of the BWRA.

metadata.section: 2. Business-wide risk assessment (as an input to the review)

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 3. Customer due diligence at onboarding (incl. EDD, PEP, beneficial ownership)
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 3 kap. 4, 7–12 och 16–20 §§; FFFS 2017:11 3 kap.; the client's CDD procedure.

**Populations:** customers onboarded in the period, by risk class and channel. Team model sample: five high-risk customer files with system extracts.

**Attributes to test per file**
1. Identity verified with an accepted method and documented (incl. the time of the check, where required).
2. Representative's identity and authority verified.
3. Beneficial owner investigated (register search plus own assessment) and verified risk-based; alternative beneficial owner where none is found.
4. Purpose and intended nature obtained, with expected activity and volumes.
5. PEP and sanctions screening performed before establishment.
6. Customer risk class assigned per the model, with the reasons documented.
7. EDD performed where the risk is high: source of funds and wealth, approval at the right level, documentation.
8. CDD completed before establishment, or a documented exception within the rules.
9. Next review date set.

**Data analysis:** customers without a risk class; missing mandatory fields; PEP customers without senior approval.

**Typical findings:** the source of funds is stated by the customer but not substantiated; the reasons for the risk class are not visible; repeated full CDD at every transaction instead of risk-based updating.

metadata.section: 3. Customer due diligence at onboarding (incl. EDD, PEP, beneficial ownership)

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 4. Customer risk classification
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 2 kap. 3–5 §§; the client's model description; model validation (PTL 6 kap. 1 § 2 st.; FFFS 2017:11, 6 kap. 14 § ff. `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`).

**Tests**
- The model's risk factors reflect the BWRA and the regulatory risk factors, or the deviations are justified.
- Manual overrides documented and approved.
- Re-classification after events (alerts, FIU reports) is performed.
- The model has been validated.
- Like cases are treated alike: re-perform the classification for a sample.

**Typical findings:** too few criteria; no link to the BWRA or monitoring; manual classification without an instruction; no validation (refer to `model-validation-report`).

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 5. Ongoing due diligence (periodic and event-driven)
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 3 kap. 13 §; PTL 2 kap. 3 § 3 st.

**Populations:** reviews due in the period; trigger events.

**Tests**
- Reviews performed on time per risk class.
- Information refreshed and the risk class reconsidered.
- Event-driven reviews triggered.
- Action taken where the CDD is insufficient (restrict, terminate, report).

**Data analysis:** overdue reviews by risk class.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 6. Transaction monitoring and alert handling
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 4 kap. 1–2 §§; the client's monitoring procedure.

**Populations:** alerts generated and closed in the period; scenario list.

**Tests**
- Scenarios and thresholds linked to the BWRA's typologies.
- Alerts handled within the internal deadlines.
- Closing rationale documented and adequate.
- Escalation per procedure.
- Second-line quality assurance of alert handling.

**Data analysis:** alert ageing; closure rates by analyst; scenarios with no alerts.

**Typical findings:** no prioritisation criteria or deadlines; closure without rationale; the monitoring scope is not risk-based.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 7. Investigation and reporting to the FIU
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 4 kap. 2–3 §§ (report without delay); 6 kap. 2 § (the compliance officer is responsible for reports); the client's procedure.

**Evidence (team model):** the five latest internal reports of suspected ML/TF; the five latest FIU reports, including the CDD measures taken during and after the investigation.

**Attributes**
1. Time from trigger to the start of the investigation, and to the report.
2. Investigation steps documented (EDD, information requests).
3. The decision to report or not, with reasoning, by the authorised role.
4. Report content complete.
5. Customer handled after reporting: risk class reviewed, relationship decision made.
6. Deputy arrangement in place (key-person dependency).
7. Case management with access control and an audit trail.

**Typical findings:** no red thread from alert to decision; flagged cases closed without documenting why the suspicion was dispelled; reporting depends on one person.

metadata.section: 7. Investigation and reporting to the FIU

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 8. Sanctions screening
description:
**Criteria:** EU and UN sanctions regimes and national rules; AMLR Art. 20(1)(d) and the RTS on CDD (screening requirements) for AMLR readiness `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.

**Tests**
- Lists are complete and updated without delay.
- Customers and beneficial owners screened at onboarding, on list changes and on data changes.
- Fuzzy-matching settings justified.
- Hits handled and the rationale documented.
- Escalation and freezing procedure in place.

**Data analysis:** a test file of known names, if agreed.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 9. Training
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 2 kap. 14 §; FFFS 2017:11 2 kap. 5–6 §§.

**Tests**
- Training content based on the BWRA and adapted to roles.
- The board is trained.
- Regular information on trends, patterns and methods.
- Records with content, participants and date.
- Completion rates for a sample of relevant roles.

**Typical findings:** only a generic e-learning course; no role-based content; incomplete records.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 10. Staff, whistleblowing and protection
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 2 kap. 13 och 15 §§; PTL 6 kap. 4 § `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`; FFFS 2017:11 2 kap. 4 och 7 §§.

**Tests**
- Suitability checks for relevant roles (sample of recent hires).
- Threat analysis performed and used.
- Whistleblowing channel working and known to staff.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 11. Outsourcing, reliance, agents and distributors
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 3 kap. 21–24 §§; outsourcing rules; AMLR provisions on agents and distributors `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.

**Tests**
- Agreements specify the AML duties.
- Oversight and testing of the providers or agents performed.
- Access to CDD data on request.

canonical_name: Compliance review report blueprint — Test programme by review area — 12. Record keeping and authority enquiries
description:
**Criteria:** PTL 5 kap. 3–4 §§ (retention); PTL 4 kap. 6–7 §§ (enquiries, system for prompt answers); FFFS 2017:11 5 kap.

**Tests**
- Retrieve a sample of records within the agreed time.
- Retention periods applied.
- A test enquiry (who held relationships with person X in the last five years) can be answered promptly and fully.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Change management for AML/CTF models
description: Reference catalogue `references/change-management.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-documentation` (skill fcp-bp-model-documentation). Sections: Introduction; 1. Significant versus other changes; 2. Workflow (team standard); 3. Model change validation request form (team template); 4. Optimisation and adjustment log (team template)

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Change management for AML/CTF models — Introduction
description: Used by: `model-documentation` (step 11; template Appendix A). Sw. *förändringshantering*.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Change management for AML/CTF models — 1. Significant versus other changes
description:
**Significant change** (Sw. *väsentlig förändring*), the team's standard definition: a change that affects the underlying purpose of the model, has a significant impact on the model's assumptions, design or data input, or otherwise significantly affects the model's output.

| Change | Typically | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| New model, or model replaced (new system) | Significant | Full documentation, validation before go-live, adoption by SAE |
| New risk category, change of model type (e.g. score-adding → weighted), new ML component | Significant | Validation before implementation |
| New or removed scenario or risk factor; change of weights or class bands | Significant, unless the MRM instruction defines a materiality threshold | Change validation request; validation; SAE decision |
| Threshold tuning within the documented rationale and tested range | Normally not significant | Test, log, SAE or delegate decision |
| Update of input lists defined as model inputs (country risk list, industry list) under an approved process | Not significant if the method is unchanged | Log; a defined latency (e.g. effective within one month) is acceptable if documented |
| New data source, or a change in data mapping that affects output | Significant if output is affected | Test in test environment first; validation as needed |
| Temporary override or deactivation (e.g. extraordinary alert flows) | Not a model change, but must be controlled | SAE decision, time limit, validator informed, log |
| Editorial update of the documentation | Not significant | Version table |

When in doubt, treat a change as significant. A significant change also triggers reassessment of the model risk and an update of the inventory.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Change management for AML/CTF models — 2. Workflow (team standard)
description:
1. **Trigger:** validation or result analysis, BWRA update, regulatory change, new product or system, investigation feedback, or a data issue.
2. **Problem statement:** what is wrong or missing, and its background.
3. **Situation-based test process:** test design in a test environment that mirrors production, including above-the-line and below-the-line testing (TM), a full-base simulation (CRC), or a name-variation test (screening).
4. **Suggested solution:** presented by the model owner's delegate (AML specialist or AFC lead) to the model owner.
5. **Change validation request:** for significant changes, the form in section 3 is sent to the validation function or the AML/CFT forum.
6. **Decision:** the SAE adopts or rejects. Some clients give the compliance or risk function a veto on deactivation.
7. **Implementation:** under the client's release and change routines, with acceptance by the model owner before production.
8. **Log and update:** the optimisation and adjustment log, the model documentation (version table), the inventory and, if relevant, the MRA.
9. **Post-implementation review:** compare the outcome with the expected effect at the next evaluation.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Customer risk classification: design and risk factor catalogue — Introduction
description: Used by: `model-documentation` (section 6 and variant 7A). Use this file to check completeness and to structure the documentation. **Include only the factors the client actually uses.** Factors in the BWRA but not in the model go to "Excluded risk factors" with their compensating control. No scores in this file come from a client; every score in a deliverable comes from the client's configuration.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Customer risk classification: design and risk factor catalogue — 1. Model design typology (for 6.1.1)
description:
| Design | How it works | When it is proportionate | Watch-outs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dominant-factor model | Single factors set the class | Rarely; supervisors do not favour it | No differentiation within classes |
| Score-adding model | Points per factor are summed; class bands decide the class | Low complexity, few products, homogeneous customers | Hard to adapt to product changes; "weighted" in name but all weights equal 1 |
| Risk-weighted model | Factors are grouped in categories; category scores are weighted and combined | Broader product range or customer types; consistent with the EBA risk factor guidelines | Weights need a documented rationale; check that no single factor dominates and that High is reachable |
| AI/ML (e.g. logistic regression on behaviour similar to FIU-reported customers) | A probabilistic score from many data points | As a complement for advanced institutions, or better as a TM behavioural model | Needs very good data quality; finds its own rules, so it cannot be stand-alone |
| Multi-component (rules + ML + manual), highest component wins | Each component sets a class; the customer gets the highest | Large banks | Document the dominance of components and prioritisation |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Customer risk classification: design and risk factor catalogue — 2. Categories and typical factors
description:
| Category | Typical factors (options) | Risk direction notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Customer** | Customer type / legal form (natural person, sole trader, limited company, partnership, foundation, non-profit association, religious community, public body, listed company, unknown form); length of relationship; complex ownership or control structure; bearer shares or nominee shareholders; industry risk (NACE/SNI list); cash-intensive business; occupation and employment sector; PEP/RCA (customer, beneficial owner, board); background check hits (court records, credit-bureau anomalies); adverse media; on internal suspicion list or FIU-reported; met in person | Public bodies and listed companies can be risk-reducing. Unknown legal form or legal form not investigated → unacceptable or undetermined. Relationship length increases risk at the start and reduces it when established without deviations |
| **Country and geography** | Address country; tax residence; citizenship; establishment of a legal entity (subsidiary, branch); EU high-risk third country connection; country risk list (internal, derived from the BWRA and public indices); intent to send or receive cross-border payments, and to which countries; domestic high-risk areas (optional) | A high-risk third country connection is a legal mandatory high (minimum value). Citizenship should not be decisive alone, but must be assessed with other factors |
| **Products and services** | Product with the highest risk held; account or service level (e.g. discretionary or advisory versus execution only); cross-border payments; third-party payments; currency exchange; credit | Where a customer has several products, document whether only the highest counts |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Customer risk classification: design and risk factor catalogue — 2. Categories and typical factors
description:
| Category | Typical factors (options) | Risk direction notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Distribution channel** | Remote or face-to-face on-boarding; identification method (e-ID, passport, by phone); partner or broker channel; office or segment belonging | Some systems cannot weight channel; then document it as add-on or risk-reducing |
| **Purpose and nature** | Stated purpose of relationship; expected volumes; source of funds and wealth (e.g. "other sales", "other loans", from a foreign bank or insurer) | Often a separate low-weight category that highlights the link between products and use |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Customer risk classification: design and risk factor catalogue — 3. Complementary methods
description:
| Method | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum value ("minimum mandatory high") | Legal or policy factors that must give at least High | PEP/RCA; high-risk third country. The customer still receives the factor's score and can reach a higher class |
| Exact value | Fixed class irrespective of the score | FIU-reported customer; legacy class carried over during transition |
| Add-on | Points added to the weighted score | New relationship (e.g. under 12 months); partner channel; third-party payments |
| Risk-reducing | Points deducted | Listed on a regulated market; public body; supervised financial institution |
| Unacceptable | The relationship may not be started or continued | True sanctions hit; bearer shares where excluded by risk appetite |
| Undetermined | KYC is insufficient to classify | Sanctions screening not performed; legal form unknown; BO identification missing |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Customer risk classification: design and risk factor catalogue — 4. Missing data (team rule)
description:
1. For each factor, state the "score when data is missing" (*Riskpoäng vid saknad data*), or state "not applicable: data always present".
2. Default for non-critical factors: the score of the **most frequent observed answer** for that factor, **plus an uncertainty add-on**. Size the add-on so that it moves a customer within a class rather than across classes `[ASSUMPTION: calibrate per client]`.
3. Risk-reducing factors with missing data are scored as if the risk-reducing attribute is absent, with no add-on.
4. Critical factors with missing data → class *Undetermined*.
5. Test the effect: initial runs where missing data took the highest score gave a disproportionate share of High, Very high and Undetermined customers. Document the analysis and the transitional decision, and plan collection of the missing data.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Customer risk classification: design and risk factor catalogue — 5. Test design for CRC
description:
- A **model blueprint** (intended purpose, functionality and factors) before calibration.
- **Test cases per class and customer category:** at least four documented cases per class (Low, Normal, High, Very high) for natural and legal persons. Cover single factors and combinations, and the extremes.
- **Re-creatable test data** (scripts or saved files), so the same cases can be rerun after a change.
- A **full customer-base run** to estimate the class distribution, plus **sample checks** of individual customers per class.
- **Sensitivity:** vary one factor or weight at a time against the base and identify the drivers. Run as workshops with AML specialists and quantitative support, using a simulation tool.
- **End-to-end checks** where the model is fed by digital KYC forms: input arrives correctly, the score is correct for the given answers, and errors are handled.
- **Expected-result checks:** FIU-reported customers concentrate in higher classes; no single factor dominates; High is reachable.
