| DR-11 | Data quality controls: reconciliation reports, incident logs for data loads (12 months), sample test results | All | Data quality assurance |
| DR-12 | Test plans, test cases, UAT sign-off, implementation test results, sensitivity analyses | All | Test sections |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Data request, interviews and workshops — 1. Data request list
description:
| ID | Item | Applies to | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| DR-13 | Statistics, 12 months: class distribution (total and per segment); alerts, cases and FIU reports per scenario; FIU reports per class; screening hits per category; handling times; overrides | All | Evaluation and suitability |
| DR-14 | Previous validation reports, internal audit reports, supervisory findings; remediation plans and status | All | Limitations, future development |
| DR-15 | Planned changes: product launches, system changes, remediation programme | All | Future development |
| DR-16 | Client document template and terminology list | All | Layout and terms |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Data request, interviews and workshops — 2. Interviews (45–60 minutes each)
description:
**Model owner (SAE)**
- What should the model achieve, and how would you know it does?
- Which changes have you decided on in the last year, and on what basis?
- How are overrides decided and documented, and who is informed?
- Which limitations do you accept, and which must be remediated?
- How is the model reported to management and the board?

**AML specialist / AFC lead (calibrates the model)**
- Walk through the logic from data in to output out.
- For each threshold, score or weight, why this value? What analysis supports it?
- What was tested at implementation, and where is the evidence?
- Which parameters does the system *not* allow you to set? Which workarounds exist?
- How are new risks from the BWRA translated into factors or scenarios?
- Which scenarios or factors do you consider ineffective, and why are they still active?

**Investigators / KYC analysts (users)**
- Which alerts or classifications are most often wrong, and in which direction?
- Which suspicious patterns do you see that the model does not catch?
- How do you record overrides, and how often do they happen?
- Is the information you need to assess an alert available in the system?

**IT / data owner / system owner**
- Data sources, frequencies and file flows; who compiles and who sends each file.
- What controls detect a failed or incomplete transfer, and who is alerted?
- Known data limitations, e.g. missing fields, free text, duplicate customers across systems.
- Test environment: how close is it to production data?
- Access management, logging, continuity.

**Supplier (if useful)**
- Standard scenario types or scoring logic, configurable versus fixed elements, release process, and notice of changes that affect the client's integration.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Data request, interviews and workshops — 3. Workshops
description:
| Workshop | Participants | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage workshop (2–3 h) | AML specialists, model owner, BWRA owner | BWRA-to-model mapping with Yes / Partly / No / Other control; gap list; reverse-gap list |
| Calibration and sensitivity workshops (CRC: several sessions over 2–3 weeks) | AML team, quantitative support, IT | Calibrated scores and weights; driver analysis; missing-data rules; expected distribution |
| Scenario tuning workshop (TM) | AML specialists, investigators | Above-the-line/below-the-line findings; threshold rationale; scenarios to deactivate or design |
| Draft review (1–2 h) | Model owner, AML specialist, validation function as observer | Agreed limitations and suitability wording; list of open `[DATA NEEDED]` |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Evaluation metrics (KPI/KRI) for AML/CTF models
description: Reference catalogue `references/evaluation-metrics.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-documentation` (skill fcp-bp-model-documentation). Sections: Introduction; 1. Definitions; 2. By model type; 3. Default CRC tolerance table (team standard; calibrate per client); 4. TM targets: how to set them; 5. Wording

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Evaluation metrics (KPI/KRI) for AML/CTF models — Introduction
description:
Used by: `model-documentation` (section 6.6; SKILL.md section 7.3). Group the metrics into the team's three categories:
1. **System functionality**
2. **Operational functionality**
3. **Assumptions and design**

Every metric in the deliverable needs a definition, a frequency, an owner and, for KRIs, a target with tolerance bands.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Evaluation metrics (KPI/KRI) for AML/CTF models — 1. Definitions
description:
| Metric | Formula / definition |
|---|---|
| Alert-to-report ratio (Sw. *FIPO-larmkvot*) | FIU reports ÷ alerts, per scenario and in total, for a period (normally 12 months) |
| Alert-to-investigation ratio | Alerts escalated to investigation or EDD ÷ alerts |
| Investigation-to-report ratio (Sw. *FIPO-utredningskvot*), if needed | FIU reports ÷ alerts that went to in-depth investigation |
| False-positive rate | Alerts closed as unfounded at first level ÷ alerts |
| FIU rate per risk class | FIU-reported customers in class ÷ customers in class |
| FIU share per risk class | FIU-reported customers in class ÷ all FIU-reported customers |
| Risk-class distribution | Share of customers per class, in total and per segment, product and country |
| Error assessment (sample) | Share of sampled Normal customers that, by expert assessment, should be High, and vice versa |
| Override rate | Manual corrections or overrides ÷ customers or alerts; split into upgrades and downgrades |
| Handling time | Time from alert to decision, against target (e.g. initial investigation within 48 hours; sanctions the same working day) |
| Backlog | Number of unhandled alerts, and their age |
| Hit ratio (screening back-test) | Test names found ÷ test names, separately for unmanipulated and manipulated names |
| ML component (if any) | Recall, accuracy, score distribution and drift, retraining date |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Evaluation metrics (KPI/KRI) for AML/CTF models — 2. By model type
description:
| Model | System functionality | Operational functionality | Assumptions and design |
|---|---|---|---|
| CRC | Failed batches and interfaces; customers without a class or with Undetermined | KYC refresh on time per class; override rate | Class distribution against target; FIU share and rate per class; error assessment both ways; missing-data share per factor |
| TM | Failed batches; data-load reconciliation differences | Handling time against target; backlog; share handled within the time set per risk class | Scenario contribution to investigations; scenario contribution to FIU reports; alert-to-report and alert-to-investigation ratio per scenario; days from alert to report (min/median/max) |
| Screening | Failed list and customer file loads | Handling time per alert type; share not closed at first level | Hits per category; true hits; back-test hit ratios; auto-closure sample results |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Evaluation metrics (KPI/KRI) for AML/CTF models — 3. Default CRC tolerance table (team standard; calibrate per client)
description:
| Metric (KRI) | Target | Low impact | Medium impact | High impact | Action required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Share of high-risk customers | [client target %] | ± 0–2 pp | ± 2–4 pp | ± 4–6 pp | ± >6 pp |
| FIU-reported customers: share in high risk | 50% | 40–50% | 30–40% | 20–30% | <20% |
| Error assessment: Normal → High | 5% | 5–10% | 10–15% | 15–20% | >20% |
| Error assessment: High → Normal | 5% | 5–10% | 10–15% | 15–20% | >20% |

- **Use:** the first two metrics for continuous follow-up, the last two for in-depth checks at validation or in sample controls. The action depends on the impact level of the deviation.
- **Setting the target share of high-risk customers:** base it on the BWRA exposure and the customer base. Do not import another client's figure. A very low share combined with a low FIU share in high risk signals under-classification.

metadata.section: 3. Default CRC tolerance table (team standard; calibrate per client)

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Evaluation metrics (KPI/KRI) for AML/CTF models — 4. TM targets: how to set them
description:
- Set one overall target and, as the model matures, one per scenario.
- Do not use an industry benchmark without a verifiable source. Set the target from the client's own data, products and investigation history, and justify any departure by product simplicity, investigation quality or tuning history.
- Both a too low and a too high alert-to-report ratio trigger review. Too high suggests reportable activity below the thresholds.
- In the first year on a new platform, it is acceptable to state that quantitative targets will be set at the first evaluation, provided a qualitative objective is stated. The minimum qualitative objective is a higher reporting rate for high-risk customers than for normal-risk customers.
- Report the period and the denominators. Never give a percentage without the counts behind it.

metadata.section: 4. TM targets: how to set them

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Evaluation metrics (KPI/KRI) for AML/CTF models — 5. Wording
description:
Weak: "The model performs well."

Good: "Over the last 12 months the scenarios generated [n] alerts, of which [n] were escalated to investigation ([x] %) and [n] led to FIU reports ([y] %). Two of seven scenarios produced no report; they are under review (section 7B.4)."

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model inventory (model register)
description: Reference catalogue `references/model-inventory.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-documentation` (skill fcp-bp-model-documentation). Sections: Introduction; 1. What belongs in the inventory; 2. Columns; 3. Rules

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model inventory (model register) — Introduction
description: Used by: `model-documentation` (step 2, supporting artefact). Sw. *modellinventering / modellregister*.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model inventory (model register) — 1. What belongs in the inventory
description:
A procedure belongs in the inventory if it **automates or standardises an assessment** that the client makes to meet AML/CTF or sanctions requirements. Being called a "model" or being statistical is not the test. Apply the test broadly. Then record any exclusions with a reason.

| Typical AML/CTF model | Model type (inventory value) | Often overlooked because |
|---|---|---|
| Customer risk classification (CRC/CRR) | Risk classification | — |
| Transaction monitoring, batch | Transaction monitoring | — |
| Real-time transaction rules (e.g. stopping outflows linked to fraud proceeds) | Transaction monitoring (real-time) | Owned by fraud or payments, not by AML |
| PEP and sanctions screening of customers, beneficial owners and representatives | Customer screening | Seen as a "system", not a model |
| Payment screening | Payment screening | Run by the payments function |
| Country risk model or country risk list feeding other models | Risk classification (input model) | Updated as a "list", outside change control |
| Industry (NACE/SNI) risk list | Risk classification (input model) | As above |
| BWRA scoring method (likelihood × impact, inherent → residual) | Risk assessment | Seen as a document, not a model |
| Alert-scoring or prioritisation logic | Transaction monitoring (component) | Hidden inside the vendor system |
| Spreadsheet or questionnaire risk scoring (smaller entities) | Risk classification | "Just a spreadsheet" |
| ML component (e.g. behavioural similarity to FIU-reported customers) | Risk classification / TM (ML component) | Documented only by data scientists |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model inventory (model register) — 2. Columns
description:
One row per model. Sheet "Inventory", plus a sheet "Version control" (Version | Update description | Date | Name/role). The first 18 columns are the team's standard. The rest are recommended additions, marked (+).

| # | Column | Content / allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Model ID (+) | Unique, e.g. M-01. Referenced in the model documentation and the MRA |
| 2 | Model name | Exact name used in the model documentation |
| 3 | Model type | Risk classification / Transaction monitoring / Customer screening / Payment screening / Risk assessment / Other |
| 4 | Area of use | AML/CFT; Financial sanctions; both |
| 5 | Risk category | AML/CFT; Financial sanctions |
| 6 | Status | Under development / Live / Under remediation / Inactive |
| 7 | Active since | Date, or "first scenarios active since [date]; see scenario documentation" |
| 8 | Inactive since | Date or N/A |
| 9 | Version | Model version, e.g. v 1.0; "Unknown" is a finding, not a value to accept |
| 10 | Model owner | Role (normally the SAE). Roles, not names, in shared copies |
| 11 | Purpose | One sentence, matching section 2 of the model documentation |
| 12 | Country | Countries where the model is used |
| 13 | Products | Products and customer segments covered |
| 14 | Dependencies to other models | Upstream and downstream models, e.g. "BWRA; CRC model; PEP/RCA screening", or "No direct dependencies; see model documentation" |
| 15 | Model criticality | Low / Normal / High / Very high (from the MRA) |
| 16 | Model quality | Low / Normal / High / Very high (from the MRA) |
| 17 | Model risk assessment (MRA) | Collected model risk from the matrix |
| 18 | MRA date of approval / MRA approved by | Date; role |
| 19 | System / supplier (+) | In-house or vendor, and module |
| 20 | Model documentation reference and version (+) | Link and version |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model inventory (model register) — 2. Columns
description:
| # | Column | Content / allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | Last independent validation (+) | Date, performed by (function), overall result |
| 22 | Next validation due (+) | Date, from the tier rule |
| 23 | Open findings (+) | Number, and the highest rating |
| 24 | Last significant change (+) | Date and change log reference |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model inventory (model register) — 3. Rules
description:
- A model not yet assessed shows "To be assessed" in columns 15–18. It must not stay like that past the next MRM reporting date.
- "Unknown" version or start date is recorded as a documentation finding.
- The inventory is owned by the MRM owner (often the SAE or the AML function). It is reviewed at least annually and whenever a model is added, significantly changed or retired.
- Retired models stay in the inventory with status Inactive and a date, so that history is traceable.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering)
description: Reference catalogue `references/model-risk-assessment.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-documentation` (skill fcp-bp-model-documentation). Sections: Introduction; 1. Workbook layout; 2. Criticality areas (how much harm a model failure could do); 3. Quality areas (how well the model works today); 4. Matrix (team standard); 5. Consequences per model risk (proposed) `[TO CONFIRM against the client's MRM instruction]`; 6. When to reassess

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering) — Introduction
description:
Used by: `model-documentation` (step 3; SKILL.md section 7.1). Sw. *modellriskbedömning*.

The structure is the team's own: a criticality block, a quality block and a 4 × 4 matrix. The workbook is one sheet per model, with the rating scale Low / Normal / High / Very high (the library labels in `_core/risk-scales.md` §1) in drop-downs. **The descriptors in sections 2 and 3, and the tier consequences in section 5, are a proposed operationalisation. Align them with the client's MRM instruction** `[TO CONFIRM]`.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering) — 1. Workbook layout
description:
1. **Header:** "Model Risk Assessment", purpose statement, [Model], rating scale legend.
2. **Criticality assessment:** one column per assessment area, with rows Comments, Criticality rating and Collected criticality assessment.
3. **Quality assessment:** one column per assessment area, with rows Comments, Quality rating and Collected quality assessment.
4. **Collected model risk assessment:** the matrix, with the final rating in bold and a comment.
5. **Sign-off:** Model risk assessment performer (model owner); date.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering) — 2. Criticality areas (how much harm a model failure could do)
description:
| Area | Low | Normal | High | Very high |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Materiality | Small share of customers or transactions; failure has limited effect | Part of the portfolio; failure partly covered by other controls | Most customers or transactions; few compensating controls | Whole portfolio, or a direct legal obligation (e.g. asset freeze); failure means a breach |
| Area of use | Prioritisation support only | Drives CDD depth or monitoring intensity | Drives on-boarding acceptance or EDD, or generates alerts for reporting | Drives prohibitions: sanctions stop or freeze, refusal or exit |
| Complexity | Few rules, transparent | Many rules or factors; simple weighting | Weighted model with complementary methods; segmentation; scoring of alerts | Statistical or ML component; vendor black box; several interacting components |
| Documentation and transparency | Fully documented and explainable | Minor gaps | Material gaps, or logic only in the system | Logic not documented or not explainable to users |
| Input and assumptions | Few inputs from one controlled source; tested assumptions | Several sources; some expert assumptions | Many sources, manual inputs, untested expert assumptions | Critical inputs missing or unreliable; key assumptions untested |
| Dependencies on other models | None | Uses or feeds one model | Feeds several models (e.g. CRC → TM thresholds) | Errors cascade across models and reporting |
| Dependencies on business processes | One process | A few processes | KYC refresh, TM and reporting depend on it | Core processes cannot run without it |

metadata.section: 2. Criticality areas (how much harm a model failure could do)

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering) — 3. Quality areas (how well the model works today)
description:
The scale direction is "Very high" = best quality.

| Area | Evidence to look at |
|---|---|
| Performance/precision | False-positive rate, alert-to-report ratio, alert-to-investigation ratio, auto-closure rate |
| Accuracy/predictability | FIU share in higher classes, sample error assessment (Normal↔High), back-test hit ratio |
| Stability/sensitivity | Stability of the class distribution and alert volumes over time; sensitivity to parameter changes; missing-data effects |
| Reliability | Batch failures, interface incidents, downtime, unprocessed alerts |
| Input data | Completeness and accuracy tests, known data limitations |
| Assumptions | Whether assumptions are documented and tested |
| Implementation | Implemented as designed; UAT and implementation testing evidenced; change control applied |

Rate each area. Then set the collected rating by judgement, and state in the comment which areas drive it. For a model not yet live, base quality on design and test evidence and write "provisional".

metadata.section: 3. Quality areas (how well the model works today)

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering) — 4. Matrix (team standard)
description:
| Model quality ↓ / Model criticality → | Very high | High | Normal | Low |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Very high** | Normal | Low | Low | Low |
| **High** | High | Normal | Normal | Low |
| **Normal** | Very high | High | Normal | Normal |
| **Low** | Very high | Very high | High | High |

*Mark the final risk assessment in bold.* Colours if used: Very high = red, High = orange, Normal = yellow, Low = green, always shown with the label.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering) — 5. Consequences per model risk (proposed) `[TO CONFIRM against the client's MRM instruction]`
description:
| Model risk | Documentation depth | Independent validation | Ongoing monitoring | Approval of significant changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Very high | Full template including all appendices; restricted specification | Before go-live and at least annually | Monthly KPI/KRI follow-up | SAE, after validation; information to management |
| High | Full template | At least annually | Quarterly | SAE, after validation |
| Normal | Full template; appendices may be lighter | At least every second year, or targeted | Semi-annual | SAE; validation of the change |
| Low | Short form (sections 1–6, 8, 13) | Every two to three years, or with BWRA review | Annual | Model owner's delegate; log entry |

metadata.section: 5. Consequences per model risk (proposed) `[TO CONFIRM against the client's MRM instruction]`

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Model risk assessment (tiering) — 6. When to reassess
description:
- After a significant change, a validation, a material incident or a BWRA update.
- At least annually, together with the inventory review.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — PEP and sanctions screening: documentation and testing
description: Reference catalogue `references/screening.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-documentation` (skill fcp-bp-model-documentation). Sections: Introduction; 1. What the screening documentation must state; 2. Match categories (generic structure); 3. Name-variation test set (back-testing and sensitivity); 4. Typical screening limitations to document; 5. KPIs

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — PEP and sanctions screening: documentation and testing — Introduction
description: Used by: `model-documentation` (section 6 and variant 7C). For the client's sanctions exposure itself, see `sanctions-risk-assessment`.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — PEP and sanctions screening: documentation and testing — 1. What the screening documentation must state
description:
| Topic | Content |
|---|---|
| Lists | Which lists are used for sanctions (EU consolidated list is mandatory in the EU; national lists; UN; others per risk appetite, e.g. OFAC or UK, stated as a choice) and for PEP/RCA; source and update frequency; known coverage gaps (RCAs especially); assessment of list-quality risk |
| Who is screened | Customers, beneficial owners, representatives, board members, signatories; counterparties in payments; suppliers if in scope |
| When | Before the relationship is established, ideally (document the gap if screening only happens after on-boarding); ongoing (e.g. daily, or delta screening on list or customer data change); payments in real time |
| Matching | Method (fuzzy matching), threshold settings, identifiers used (national ID number, date of birth, country), match categories and their handling |
| Alert handling | Handling time targets (sanctions alerts same working day; PEP within a set time); weekend handling; escalation; freezing and reporting of true sanctions hits |
| False-positive suppression | Investigated false positives do not re-alert until list or customer data changes; documented rationale |
| Auto-closure | Any auto-archived low-quality categories, with rationale and periodic sample testing |
| Downstream use | How PEP/RCA or sanctions status flows into CRC (minimum or unacceptable value), manually or automatically |
| Optional controls | IP geolocation and blocking of sanctioned jurisdictions; VPN detection |

metadata.section: 1. What the screening documentation must state

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — PEP and sanctions screening: documentation and testing — 2. Match categories (generic structure)
description:
Vendors use their own category schemes. Document the client's scheme in this form:

| Category | Typical meaning | Typical handling |
|---|---|---|
| Identifier match | Personal or company ID number matches the list entry | Highest priority |
| Full primary-name match | Customer name matches the primary name; middle names may be missing | Investigate |
| Alias / former-name / spelling-variant match | Match against AKA, FKA or spelling variants | Investigate |
| Initial-based match | List entry or customer name contains initials | Investigate |
| Partial-name match | Only first or only last name matches; list entry lacks a full name | Often auto-closed: **justify and sample-test** |
| Name-type mismatch | Match on a name component in an unusual position | Often auto-closed: **justify and sample-test** |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — PEP and sanctions screening: documentation and testing — 3. Name-variation test set (back-testing and sensitivity)
description:
Test the model's ability to find listed names both unchanged and with deviations. The team's variation types:

1. Phonetic similarity
2. Transliteration spelling differences
3. Nicknames
4. Missing spaces and hyphens
5. Titles and honorifics
6. Truncated name components
7. Missing name components
8. Out-of-order name components
9. Initials
10. Names split inconsistently across database fields
11. Same name in multiple languages
12. Semantically similar names
13. Semantically similar names across languages

Set explicit **hit-ratio targets** for unmanipulated and manipulated names before testing. The team has used targets in the high nineties (percent) for unmanipulated names and a materially lower, still defined, target for manipulated names `[TO CONFIRM per client]`. Record the false-positive volume at the chosen setting. Repeat after any threshold or list change.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — PEP and sanctions screening: documentation and testing — 4. Typical screening limitations to document
description:
- Detection depends on listed persons acting under a listed name. Circumvention through structures or front persons is not caught by name screening; refer to CDD and ownership analysis.
- No date-of-birth or ID logic, so the model relies on fuzzy names plus manual investigation.
- PEP lists may contain errors and omissions, especially for RCAs.
- Customer names may be wrong in the source system; describe the name verification at on-boarding.
- Screening only after on-boarding (e.g. the first night), so a sanctioned person could be on-boarded.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — PEP and sanctions screening: documentation and testing — 5. KPIs
description: System failures and failed list or customer file loads; alerts per category; false-positive rate; handling time against target per alert type; share of hits not closed at first level; true hits and freezes; back-test hit ratios.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields
description: Reference catalogue `references/tm-scenarios.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-documentation` (skill fcp-bp-model-documentation). Sections: Introduction; 1. Monitoring methods (for 6.1.1 and 7B.2.1); 2. Typologies by product (catalogue); 3. Scenario documentation fields (for 7B.3 and the scenario log); 4. Design, optimisation and deactivation (for 7B.2.2); 5. Manual override in TM; 6. Alert-volume benchmark (optional sanity check)

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — Introduction
description: Used by: `model-documentation` (section 6 and variant 7B). This is a completeness check, not content to paste. Document only the scenarios the client runs. Typologies the client faces but does not monitor go to "Gaps in scenarios". No thresholds in this file come from a client; every threshold in a deliverable comes from the client's configuration, with its rationale.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — 1. Monitoring methods (for 6.1.1 and 7B.2.1)
description:
| Method | What it detects | Fits | Limitation to document |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rule-based, fixed thresholds (amount, volume, frequency) | Transactions above set limits | Simple products and low volumes | Activity just below the threshold is missed; inflexible |
| Typology / modus scenarios | Known patterns, e.g. many deposits followed by withdrawal | Products with few possible actions | Needs an up-to-date typology base; new modi are missed |
| Deviation from KYC | Activity larger or different from what the customer stated | Deposits and transaction accounts | Answers given at on-boarding may not predict long-term use |
| Deviation from own history | Change versus the customer's average behaviour | Most products; reduces repeat alerts | New customers lack history |
| Deviation from peer group / segment | Behaviour unusual for similar customers | Larger, diverse portfolios; needs segmentation | Segment design must be documented |
| Behaviour-based / statistical | Similarity to previously reported behaviour | Advanced institutions | Data and resource heavy; explainability |
| Real-time rules | Stop high-risk outflows before execution | Payment-intensive businesses; fraud-linked laundering | Usually not required by law; document the scope choice |

Document whether **customer risk class** adjusts scenarios, e.g. lower thresholds or higher alert scores for higher classes. A team pattern is risk-tiered relative thresholds. For example, the extra-amortisation threshold is set as a percentage of the planned amortisation and falls as the risk class rises, combined with outstanding debt, loan age and the customer's turnover or liquidity, and the latest KYC is considered for High and Very high.

Document any **segmentation**: product → purpose of relationship → employment status (e.g. employed / retired / other), each segment with its own calibrated thresholds.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — 2. Typologies by product (catalogue)
description:
| Product / business | Typologies and red flags to consider |
|---|---|
| Consumer loans and credit accounts | Large or early repayment without plausible explanation; repeated early repayments; overpayment beyond contract; refund of overpayment, especially to an account other than the paying one; frequent orders of goods on credit with matching payments; credit maxed out on goods and never repaid (possible TF/fraud); young customers recruited to take credit for others |
| Mortgages | Extra amortisation (single large, or frequent); aggressive payment plans; third party without apparent link paying; purchase at non-market value; large gap between declared and assessed income |
| Deposit / savings accounts | Several deposits followed by a significant withdrawal; deposit larger than stated in KYC; high number of transactions (structuring); account emptied shortly after each deposit; deposits from multiple sources; high turnover; PEP customers via partner channels |
| Transaction accounts | Unaware or aware money mules: new account with incoming funds quickly sent abroad; activity in a dormant account; flow-through of funds; key words in payment messages linked to known fraud schemes; excessive instant mobile payments in or out; deviation from historical volume or value; salary deposits versus stated income |
| Cards and cash | ATM withdrawals and card purchases in high-risk or TF-linked countries; purchases with merchant category codes linked to TF preparation |
| Cross-border payments | Payments to or from high-risk countries; third-party payments; payments not matching KYC intent |
| Leasing (B2B) | Large or early payments; overpayments; payments out of line with the customer's profile |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — 2. Typologies by product (catalogue)
description:
| Product / business | Typologies and red flags to consider |
|---|---|
| Securities and custody | Securities transferred in and quickly out to several institutions; flow-through of securities or cash; trading that lacks economic sense or imitates trading; indifference to costs; off-market or block trades at off-market prices |
| Life insurance and pensions | Early surrender or repurchase; change of beneficiary; premium overpayment and refund; pension contributions not in line with the company's finances |
| Payment and e-money institutions | Velocity; many-to-one and one-to-many flows; merchant refunds without sales; agent or distributor anomalies |

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — 3. Scenario documentation fields (for 7B.3 and the scenario log)
description:
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Scenario ID and name | e.g. SC-03 Overpayment above threshold |
| Customer segment / product | |
| Purpose | What behaviour the scenario aims to detect |
| Risk / typology covered | BWRA reference; table of Typology/Product/Risk factor and Red flags |
| Scenario type and logic | Vendor scenario type or own rule; look-back period; filters |
| Parameters and thresholds | Per segment or risk class |
| Threshold rationale | Normal behaviour for the product (e.g. typical credit size), analysis performed, external input |
| Expected volume and alert-to-report ratio | Target per scenario |
| Initial investigative measures | What the investigator checks first |
| Known limitations | e.g. normal refinancing triggers alerts; cannot use payee data |
| Last tuned / last evaluated | Date, result |
| Status | Active / In test / Deactivated (date, decision) |

metadata.section: 3. Scenario documentation fields (for 7B.3 and the scenario log)

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — 4. Design, optimisation and deactivation (for 7B.2.2)
description:
- **Design inputs:** BWRA and the analysis behind it; FIU and authority reports and statistics; information from peers and industry; supplier knowledge; investigators' and product staff's knowledge of normal and suspicious behaviour.
- **Design steps:**
  1. Understand the modus and the data points it needs.
  2. Choose a scenario type; if none fits, consider data adjustments or a type meant for another purpose.
  3. Analyse the general customer base to minimise overlap with normal behaviour.
  4. Run in a test environment that mirrors production.
  5. Perform above-the-line and below-the-line testing on all key parameters.
  6. Get acceptance by the model owner.
  7. Implement.
  8. Log the change.
- **Optimisation:** a formal evaluation at least annually, plus ongoing follow-up. An alert-to-report ratio significantly below *or above* target triggers review: a very high ratio suggests hits are being missed below the threshold. Recalibrate or replace.
- **Deactivation:** an ineffective scenario is phased out. If not replaced, the SAE approves and the remaining risk is managed otherwise. Log it.
- **The quality measure and its caveat:** the alert-to-report ratio is the best available measure, but the absence of FIU feedback limits it. Say so.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — 5. Manual override in TM
description: Override covers temporary exclusion of scenarios for a customer, deviations from the predefined investigation, or temporary deactivation in extraordinary situations (e.g. macroeconomic events flooding alerts). Each override needs a documented justification, a time limit and an SAE decision, and the validation function must be informed. Overrides feed the scenario evaluation. Some systems let investigators raise the alert score for a customer and scenario instead of closing; document that as well.

canonical_name: Model documentation (TM, screening, customer risk classification) blueprint — Transaction monitoring: methods, scenario catalogue and documentation fields — 6. Alert-volume benchmark (optional sanity check)
description: The team has a method to estimate a reasonable alert volume from public data. It needs an assumed alert-to-report ratio, which must come from a verifiable source or the client's own history (do not use an industry benchmark without a verifiable source), and uses regression on the supervisor's risk score for the entity and its number of employees, with a confidence interval. It is best suited to mid-sized and smaller institutions. Use it only as a discussion point on whether alert volume and the alert-to-report ratio are plausible. Never present it as a target, and refresh the underlying data before use `[TO CONFIRM: current data year]`.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations
description: Reference catalogue `references/assessment-areas.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-validation-report` (skill fcp-bp-model-validation-report). Sections: Introduction; 1.1 Documentation (*Dokumentation*); 1.2 Business objectives (*Affärsmål / Modellens mål*); 1.3 Process for model use (*Process för modellanvändning*); 1.4 Criteria and design for model monitoring (*Kriterier och design för modellövervakning*); 1.5 Process for model selection (*Process för val av modell*); 1.6 Method (*Metod / Metodik*); 1.7 Process for selecting risk factors / scenarios and thresholds / lists and matching rules (*Process för val av riskfaktorer / scenarier och tröskelvärden*); 1.8 Management's process for overrides, incl. roles and responsibilities (*Ledningens process för åsidosättande, inkl. roller och ansvar*); 1.9 Governance (*Styrning*); 1.10 Data (*Data*); 1.11 Model limitations and assumptions (*Modellbegränsningar och antaganden*); 2.1 Test plan, testing and data (*Testplan, testning och data*); 2.2 Change management (*Förändringsledning*); 3.1 Data, complete and correct (*Data, komplett och korrekt*); 3.2 Missing data/compensation (*Avsaknad av data/kompensation*); 4.1 Sensitivity (*Känslighet*); 4.2 Limitations and assumptions (*Begränsningar och antaganden*); 4.3 Model effectiveness (*Modelleffektivitet*); 4.4 Quantitative and qualitative validation (*Kvantitativ och kvalitativ validering*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — Introduction
description:
Used by: `model-validation-report`. One block per sub-area, in the team's report order. Each block gives:

- **Expectation** – the standard text for the Expectation/requirement column (normally the model owner's responsibility). Adapt the wording to the model type.
- **VT – initial** – what the validation team (VT) does in an initial (full) validation.
- **VT – ongoing** – what the VT does in an ongoing validation.
- **Anchor (SE)** – the reference used in the team's work programme for Sweden, with its type: *more direct legal requirement*, *indirect legal requirement*, or *no direct reference, complements the MRM framework*. All Swedish references: `[VERIFY REFERENCE]` against current texts. For other jurisdictions, replace through `{{jurisdiction}}`.
- **Evidence and typical findings.**

Ratings use `rating-scale.md`. Swedish sub-area names are in parentheses.

---

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.1 Documentation (*Dokumentation*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The model shall be documented well enough for an independent third party with relevant expertise to understand how it works, identify its key features, assumptions and limitations, and replicate parameter estimates and results. The roles and responsibilities of the model owner, implementer and users shall be clearly defined. The documentation should reason about the advantages and disadvantages of the chosen design compared with alternatives, and the method should be able to accommodate change over time. For a vendor model, the model owner shall obtain documentation that enables validation (parts may be requested from the vendor); where it is not available, the owner documents the request and the refusal and supplements with in-house material.
- **VT – initial.** Review all documentation against the expectation; run the documentation analysis (expected documentation list in `data-request.md`).
- **VT – ongoing.** Check whether changes have been made that require documentation, and whether that documentation is complete.
- **Anchor (SE).** No direct reference; complements the MRM framework and supports the requirement to describe theory and assumptions in the MRM routines (FFFS 2017:11, 6 kap. 14 § ff. `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`).
- **Evidence and typical findings.** Is there a dedicated model documentation or only scattered routines? Typical Red: no dedicated model documentation; parameter lists without rationale. Recommended minimum content: purpose and business objective; roles and responsibilities; model specification (selection, structure, limitations, evaluation); account of risk factors or scenarios with the rationale for scores and thresholds; data; dependencies on other models; supporting lists (country risk, industry risk) as appendices.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.2 Business objectives (*Affärsmål / Modellens mål*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The business objective shall be clearly stated to explain the model's purpose and target outcome within the financial crime context, including an evaluation of alternatives considered and the conclusion. The BWRA should drive the business objective, which in turn drives the requirements on the model; if the model cannot meet the risks, the objective cannot be reached. The target outcome defines what the model tries to predict, with an observation period (e.g. within 12 months) and a binary, quantifiable and unique outcome (e.g. reported to the FIU or not).
  - *TM:* objectives should include measurable indicators of effectiveness, such as the share of alerts leading to in-depth investigation and the share leading to a report to the FIU.
  - *CRC:* typically the relative share of reports to the FIU or in-depth investigations in the higher risk classes (accuracy ratio).
  - *Screening:* objectives of the screening process should be relevant and quantifiable, so that actual outcomes can be compared with expected outcomes.
  - *BWRA:* not fully applicable; the objective is to form the basis for the other models and routines.
- **VT – initial.** Review and evaluate the AML business objective to ensure the model's role is clear to developers and users; assess whether the target outcome is consistent with the objective.
- **VT – ongoing.** Have the objective or target outcome changed? Are the changes reasonable?
- **Anchor (SE).** More direct legal requirement: FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, first para.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.3 Process for model use (*Process för modellanvändning*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The documentation shall explain how the model is used day to day, including how users can amend inputs and amend or override outputs, and how the model interacts with onboarding CDD, ongoing due diligence and (for CRC) transaction monitoring.
- **VT – initial.** Review the use process as described in the MRM routines, model documentation and SOPs; assess whether use is purposeful. Check that a user guide or training explains the drivers of the model.
- **VT – ongoing.** Is the use process up to date and in line with practice?
- **Anchor (SE).** No direct reference; industry guidance.
- **Typical findings.** Case-handling routine describes handling per product but not the link between product, scenario and risk factor.

metadata.section: 1.3 Process for model use (*Process för modellanvändning*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.4 Criteria and design for model monitoring (*Kriterier och design för modellövervakning*)
description:
- **Expectation.** There shall be a set procedure to review model performance against the business objective, including performance testing, and to explain limitations users should be aware of and enable improvements. Ongoing monitoring of the conceptual design (expected versus actual outcome) should use relevant KPIs/KRIs on effectiveness, investigations etc. Monitoring is typically carried out through input-data controls, measurement of downtime, IT incidents and similar controls.
- **VT – initial.** Review the requirements set in the MRM routines and model documentation for performance testing and how results inform improvements; assess whether the procedures are fit for purpose.
- **VT – ongoing.** Have there been changes that need to be considered?
- **Anchor (SE).** More direct legal requirement: PTL ch. 6, s. 1, second para.
- **Typical findings.** Evaluations happen but are not formalised (key-person dependency); KPIs reported to a committee cover stability (file-transfer errors) but not effectiveness.

metadata.section: 1.4 Criteria and design for model monitoring (*Kriterier och design för modellövervakning*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.5 Process for model selection (*Process för val av modell*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The model owner shall evaluate and document the model's conceptual soundness, including the rationale and process (underlying theories and assumptions) for selecting the model and a comparison of its ability to meet the business objective, legal requirements and the BWRA. *In-house:* more comprehensive documentation of why it is more suitable than a proven solution. *Vendor:* why the vendor was chosen, how knowledge transfer was completed, and how third-party risks were identified and mitigated.
- **VT – initial.** Review the rationale and process; determine whether the documentation is adequate and the rationale reasonable.
- **VT – ongoing.** N/A unless major changes to processes or business.
- **Anchor (SE).** More direct legal requirement: FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 14, second para., first item.

metadata.section: 1.5 Process for model selection (*Process för val av modell*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.6 Method (*Metod / Metodik*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The model owner shall evaluate the method's ability to meet the business objective, legal and regulatory requirements and the risks identified in the BWRA, and consider relevant guidance (EBA guidelines, industry practice). The documentation should include advantages and disadvantages of the chosen design and other methods considered. The method must be able to incorporate changes over time (risks in the BWRA change; risk factors, scenarios and thresholds may need to change).
- **VT – initial.** Review and challenge how the method was determined to meet the objective considering, at minimum, legal requirements; assess completeness and reasonableness of the pros and cons; evaluate flexibility to change.
- **VT – ongoing.** Changes since implementation or first validation? Remediation ongoing?
- **Anchor (SE).** Indirect (MD) / more direct (MV) legal requirement: FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, first para.
- **Judgement.** The aim is relevant coverage, not full coverage of every product and risk factor. Risks not covered by the model must be mitigated elsewhere, and that must be demonstrable. For CRC: a method that averages risk factors within a category is not flexible – adding a factor dilutes the others.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.7 Process for selecting risk factors / scenarios and thresholds / lists and matching rules (*Process för val av riskfaktorer / scenarier och tröskelvärden*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The documentation shall describe the relevant spectrum of risk factors, scenarios or parameters that should or could be available to ensure risk coverage, and the process – including the level of expert judgement – by which BWRA risks are used to choose them. This can be done through purposeful mapping, at minimum against the BWRA (which in turn should have considered the national AML act and preferably EBA guidelines and industry practice).
- **VT – initial.** Review the process and level of expert judgement; determine whether reasonable and fit for purpose. Run the gap analysis (test files per model type).
- **VT – ongoing.** Have new risks been identified in the BWRA (or externally) since the last validation, and does the model take them into account?
- **Anchor (SE).** Indirect (MD) / more direct (MV): FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, first para.

metadata.section: 1.7 Process for selecting risk factors / scenarios and thresholds / lists and matching rules (*Process för val av riskfaktorer / scenarier och tröskelvärden*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.8 Management's process for overrides, incl. roles and responsibilities (*Ledningens process för åsidosättande, inkl. roller och ansvar*)
description:
- **Expectation.** Overrides may be common in certain cases of elevated risk and, rarely, for established customers with well-known business. The process shall be described in the model documentation or routines. Overrides should be exceptional and time-limited and usually require approval by a management role; they should be subject to review and reasonableness assessment.
  - *TM:* e.g. excluding a customer who repeatedly triggers the same alert for a known reason from a specific rule; setting a scenario as dormant. Risk: affected customers are not monitored as intended.
  - *CRC:* manual adjustment of risk class. Risk: customers do not receive enhanced KYC or closer monitoring.
  - *Screening:* whitelists, good-guy lists, suppression rules. Risk: high-risk customers or sanctioned parties evade detection.
- **VT – initial.** Review the process and assess reasonableness; check whether overrides can be registered without approval and, if so, the risk this entails; for CRC sample overrides (approved, by whom, when, with a reasonable rationale; override score used downstream).
- **VT – ongoing.** Have overrides been made? Were they motivated and documented?
- **Anchor (SE).** No direct reference; complements the MRM framework.
- **Typical findings.** De facto overrides outside the process: deactivated rules without a decision log; "extra monitoring" flags that do not change the risk class. Good recommendation: workflow and criteria, roles and mandates, and a decision log (change, decision date, implementation date, time-limited or not, decision-maker).

metadata.section: 1.8 Management's process for overrides, incl. roles and responsibilities (*Ledningens process för åsidosättande, inkl. roller och ansvar*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.9 Governance (*Styrning*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The model development process and method should be aligned with internal policies, instructions, guidelines and SOPs. Roles and responsibilities of model owner, implementer and users shall be clearly defined and documented throughout the MRM framework, or referenced.
- **VT – initial.** Check how well method and processes meet internal policies; assess roles against the expectation.
- **VT – ongoing.** Changes since the last validation?
- **Anchor (SE).** No direct reference; complements the MRM framework.
- **Typical findings.** A system owner is named, but not a model owner.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.10 Data (*Data*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The model documentation shall include a description and definition of the data used (development, use and monitoring), including how missing values are treated. It should manage key-person dependency: it must be possible to identify where data comes from without relying on individuals. It should describe how lack of data is handled, either for individual data or as a model limitation. Can be done through mapping of needed/expected data flows and tests that confirm the actual flow.
- **VT – initial.** Assess the completeness of the data description (variable, source, field name, description, registration date; default values or exclusions with rationale).
- **VT – ongoing.** Changes since implementation? Remediation ongoing?
- **Anchor (SE).** More direct (MV): FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, second para.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 1.11 Model limitations and assumptions (*Modellbegränsningar och antaganden*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The BWRA is the cornerstone of all AML/CTF measures; in practice this applies especially to models, whose assumptions should as far as possible reflect the content and reasoning of the BWRA. Assumptions and limitations should be documented in full, especially assumptions about expected risk coverage relative to the objective (e.g. when setting thresholds and scores). Where exact information is lacking, an assumption based on the "average" customer in the relevant category may be made, documented with its logic and conclusion. The effect of each limitation should be analysed and the conclusion documented (does it significantly impair the model's ability to mitigate risk?). Limitations can be system constraints, missing customer data (legal right to collect) etc.
- **VT – initial.** Review completeness across the lifecycle (development, use, monitoring); assess whether the analysis is appropriate and conclusions reasonable; compare limitations with the BWRA and check whether other controls mitigate them. Include a table of key limitations and mitigants in the report for senior management awareness.
- **VT – ongoing.** Changes? Are mitigations still in place?
- **Anchor (SE).** More direct: FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 14, second para. (MD); ch. 6, s. 15, second para. (MV).
- **Typical findings.** TM rules use no KYC data (a material limitation under the AML act's monitoring requirement).

---

metadata.section: 1.11 Model limitations and assumptions (*Modellbegränsningar och antaganden*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 2.1 Test plan, testing and data (*Testplan, testning och data*)
description:
The work programme splits this into Test plan, Testing and Data; the report shows one row.
- **Expectation.** For the model to work, it must capture and receive relevant data. The undertaking needs robust testing processes, with tests before and during implementation of a model or new risk factors and throughout its life. The model owner should ensure a complete test plan covering all inputs, coding and outputs, describing planned user acceptance and operational test cases. User acceptance and functional implementation testing must be performed and documented; identified issues require evidence of remediation. Internal and external data in the use process should be evaluated for suitability, completeness and correctness; the test plan should include reasonable data tests; results should be available for review; issues should be documented with an action plan.
- **VT – initial.** Review the test plan for completeness; review training of testers; review a sample of UAT and operational test reports; check code review (who, when, outcome, issues fixed); check controls for identified risks (e.g. completeness across multiple systems, inclusion of newly launched products).
- **VT – ongoing.** Is the test plan in use? Has relevant testing taken place since the last validation, and was it reasonable?
- **Anchor (SE).** Indirect: PTL ch. 6, s. 1, second para. (testing); more direct for data: FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, second para.
- **Standard questions in the report.** Is there a test plan and is it documented; is there a training plan for case handlers? Have user tests been performed; have code and input data been tested? Has the data been tested and evaluated?

metadata.section: 2.1 Test plan, testing and data (*Testplan, testning och data*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 2.2 Change management (*Förändringsledning*)
description:
- **Expectation.** There shall be a documented and implemented process for how model changes are carried out and what analysis a change requires. It should cover all steps: idea, mapping, analysis, assumptions, limitations and dependencies, change request, implementation and test plan/testing of all inputs (incl. coding) and outputs, result analysis, approval; and name the performers (AML function, IT, vendors) and escalation routes. It should define what a significant change is (which triggers validation).
- **VT – initial.** Review whether the process is fit for purpose and followed.
- **VT – ongoing.** Have changes been made to the model or the routine? Was the routine followed? Were routine changes fit for purpose?
- **Anchor (SE).** More direct: the requirement that MRM routines describe how model changes are documented (FFFS 2017:11, 6 kap. 14 § ff.). `[VERIFY REFERENCE: the team's work programme cites "FFFS 14:1", which appears to be a typo]`
- **Typical findings.** No definition of significant change; process for pausing or switching off scenarios missing.

---

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 3.1 Data, complete and correct (*Data, komplett och korrekt*)
description:
- **Expectation.** Process and system mapping of input data should be part of the model documentation, with documentation of ongoing data quality assurance and independent validation reports. Controls shall be performed on data transfer and on data being complete and correct. Definitions of data points used or desired should be documented so a third party can understand them.
- **VT – initial.** Assess the process ensuring input data is appropriate, complete and correct; where applicable review model code to evaluate the developer's code review and development tests; assess definitions.
- **VT – ongoing.** Is the test plan in use; relevant data testing since last validation; any changes affecting the previous analysis?
- **Anchor (SE).** More direct: FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, second para.
- **Typical findings.** Controls exist (daily checks, annual review of data delivered to the system) but are not referenced in the model documentation.

metadata.section: 3.1 Data, complete and correct (*Data, komplett och korrekt*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 3.2 Missing data/compensation (*Avsaknad av data/kompensation*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The extent of missing values in the development and monitoring datasets must be analysed to understand the effect on model calibration and monitoring results. The analysis should be part of the model documentation.
- **VT – initial.** Review the owner's analysis; where appropriate perform own analysis (e.g. customers with missing data per risk factor) and conclude on the effect on results.
- **VT – ongoing.** Changes affecting the previous analysis?
- **Anchor (SE).** No direct reference; complements the MRM framework.

---

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 4.1 Sensitivity (*Känslighet*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The model's sensitivity to inputs and parameters should be tested on an ongoing basis, results documented and acted on. Where only the vendor can test fully, the owner should obtain the necessary information or assurance from the vendor.
- **VT – initial.** Review the developer's sensitivity tests and conclude; if none exist, perform own sensitivity analysis (see test files).
- **VT – ongoing.** Are there sensitivity KPIs and ongoing output monitoring?
- **Anchor (SE).** Indirect: PTL ch. 6, s. 1, second para. (MD); FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, first para. (MV).

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 4.2 Limitations and assumptions (*Begränsningar och antaganden*)
description:
- **Expectation.** Assumptions and limitations affecting output should be analysed and documented, with mitigating actions and further development where needed; analysed at development and at the annual review.
- **VT.** Review the analysis, including sensitivity and scenario analysis of their effect; review how limitations are communicated to users and how they constrain use; if missing, analyse a sample of the most material limitations.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 4.3 Model effectiveness (*Modelleffektivitet*)
description:
- **Expectation.** A documented process to verify effectiveness, allowing accurate and stable estimation at outcome, with continuous comparison of current output with previous periods. Effectiveness follow-up shall lead to action, and target levels shall be defined.
  - *TM:* scenario effectiveness in terms of reports to the FIU, in-depth investigations and false-positive alerts relative to total alerts.
  - *CRC:* more reports to the FIU and in-depth investigations in higher risk classes.
  - *Screening:* number of hits leading to further investigation or action such as blocking or suspending high-risk customers and transactions.
- **VT – initial.** Assess the process used to determine effectiveness; run the quantitative tests.
- **VT – ongoing.** Changes to the process?
- **Anchor (SE).** Indirect: PTL ch. 6, s. 1, second para.; FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, first para.
- **Judgement.** Industry thinking has moved beyond alert-to-report ratios, which measure quantity rather than usefulness. Ask also whether reports fall within national priority areas, identify networks or result from complex investigations; whether false negatives are analysed (reports originating from manual referrals); and whether resources go to observed, material typologies rather than theoretical coverage. A small, low-risk firm can have an effective programme with few or no reports if it understands its risks and has a reasonable, risk-based design.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Assessment areas, sub-areas and expectations — 4.4 Quantitative and qualitative validation (*Kvantitativ och kvalitativ validering*)
description:
- **Expectation.** The model documentation should describe quantitative factors such as completeness, correctness and stability.
- **VT – initial.** Perform qualitative and quantitative steps to validate performance, correctness, completeness and stability. Minimum per model:
  - TM: coverage against products, risks and customer categories; coverage against risk factors; ratio of alerts to reports per scenario.
  - CRC: how the CRC is used in KYC; how it is used for TM thresholds and scope; back-testing of reports to the FIU by customer risk class.
  - Screening: sample testing of name matching to confirm fuzzy logic.
  - BWRA as model: benchmark of risk levels against external sources.
  - Optional, depending on data: population stability index (PSI) for stability; ROC curve and confusion matrix (CRC); binomial or Vasicek-type tests of estimates against outcomes.
- **VT – ongoing.** Test KPIs and the owner's ongoing testing.
- **Anchor (SE).** Indirect: FFFS 2017:11, ch. 6, s. 15, first para.

metadata.section: 4.4 Quantitative and qualitative validation (*Kvantitativ och kvalitativ validering*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Documentation and data request
description: Reference catalogue `references/data-request.md` of the FCP blueprint `model-validation-report` (skill fcp-bp-model-validation-report). Sections: Introduction; 1. Kick-off meeting checklist (*Att ta upp vid första uppstartsmötet*); 2. General documents (all model types) (*Generella dokument*); 3. Transaction monitoring (*Transaktionsmonitorering*); 4. Customer risk classification (*Kundriskklassificering*); 5. Screening (*Screening/sanktionslistor*); 6. BWRA as a model; 7. Expected documentation list (used for the documentation analysis); 8. Email text (adapt to {{language}}); 9. Data handling

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Documentation and data request — Introduction
description: Used by: `model-validation-report`. Sent at kick-off as an email with the list attached or inline. Swedish title used by the team: *Inhämtande av dokumentation inför modellvalidering*.

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Documentation and data request — 1. Kick-off meeting checklist (*Att ta upp vid första uppstartsmötet*)
description:
- Which documents and data will be provided, and by when (agree dates).
- How material is transferred (secure channel; no customer data by ordinary email).
- Does the client perform manual overrides (deactivated scenarios, excluded customers, manual risk-class changes, whitelists)?
- Report language: Swedish or English.
- Does the client have its own report template (e.g. prescribed by its MRM guideline)?
- Deadline for the draft and the final report.
- Who is the model owner, who is responsible, and to whom do we report? Which function signs off?
- Initial (full) or ongoing validation? Previous validation report and status of its actions.
- Interview slots: model owner, developers/system administrators, AML analysts/investigators, IT/data.
- Is a test environment available (replication, name tests, threshold tests)?

Internal tip: for assessment areas related to data, interviews with developers and the business may be needed. Assess the need early and book the meetings in good time.

metadata.section: 1. Kick-off meeting checklist (*Att ta upp vid första uppstartsmötet*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Documentation and data request — 2. General documents (all model types) (*Generella dokument*)
description:
| # | Document | Why |
|---|---|---|

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Documentation and data request — 7. Expected documentation list (used for the documentation analysis)
description:
Ask for whatever exists under these headings; absence is a finding, not a reason to stop.

1. Process map (practical process and technical: systems and data)
2. Criteria and design for model monitoring (MRM routines and KPIs)
3. Report from ongoing model monitoring (KPIs, accuracy, reasonableness)
4. Business objective for the model (what it aims to achieve; target outcome with observation period and binary result)
5. AML/CTF risk assessment with mitigating measures; link between BWRA risk factors and scenarios/risk factors
6. Development evidence: how the model was tested, data used, and how results show it works as intended (development plan, test plan, execution, results, analysis, conclusions)
7. Model methodology: theoretical approach, assumptions, known limitations
8. Model specification: data, formulas, parameters, inputs and outputs, dependencies, processing flow, reports, dependencies on other models
9. Data for implementation, describing all fields used
10. Rules or segmentation logic with thresholds and calibration data
11. User procedures for executing and maintaining the model
12. Manual override process, incl. roles and responsibilities
13. Compliance procedure describing how outputs are used (e.g. case handling and reporting to the FIU)
14. Reporting of model output to management/board, with evidence of review and approval
15. Annual model review: continued suitability for the portfolio and current conditions
16. (TM) Alert statistics per scenario: alerts, share to in-depth investigation, share reported

Used by: `model-validation-report`. The TM battery is the team's own interview and review question set (translated and neutralised). The CRC, screening and BWRA sections are derived from the expectations in the team's work programme; extend them from experience. `[TO CONFIRM: team to review the derived sections]`

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Interview question bank — 1. Transaction monitoring (*Frågebatteri – validering av modellen för transaktionsmonitorering*)
description:
**Type of monitoring**
- How is monitoring done – manually or automated? Is there an assessment of why?
- Is there an assessment of ex-post versus real-time monitoring?
- Are regular checks made on a sample of all transactions (regardless of monitoring) to identify trends that inform the risk assessment and to test and improve the reliability and appropriateness of the TM system?

**Risk scenarios – scope and focus**
- Are all customers, products and transactions covered?
- How many alerts per product? Is that in line with the risk assessment and the size of the business?
- Are alerts generated every day? How many?
- How many scenarios are there, which ones, and which patterns do they look for? Check against a typology list, for example: excessive cash handling; account used as pass-through; excessive ATM activity; movement of funds; patterns of transfers between multiple accounts; sequence of events; structuring; unusual card use; change in account behaviour; use of dormant accounts; use of multiple jurisdictions; currency use; excessive use of online payment systems; early repayment of loan; overpayment of loan; recurring originators and beneficiaries; excessive losses; low-priced securities; journaling between (sub-)accounts; excessive cancels and corrections; redemption shortly after subscription with disregard for fees; known and unknown remitter and beneficiary names.
- Is there a scenario for every risk behaviour identified in the risk assessment?
- Are other relevant risk factors reflected (PEPs, high-risk countries, high-risk industries)?
- Is there a combination of broad and narrow scenarios?
- Are parameters/scenarios adapted to risk class or CDD level? What differs between high-risk and low-risk alerts?

metadata.section: 1. Transaction monitoring (*Frågebatteri – validering av modellen för transaktionsmonitorering*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Interview question bank — 1. Transaction monitoring (*Frågebatteri – validering av modellen för transaktionsmonitorering*)
description:
- Is monitoring adapted to the individual customer's CDD (e.g. alert against declared amount, purpose and nature – account profile inconsistent with CDD profile)?
- Is customer behaviour compared with peers in the same segment?
- Is machine learning used?
- Can customers be flagged in the system? Are previously reported customers reviewed more closely? Does a previous review affect review frequency?
- How many transactions/activities are reported to the FIU each year? How many transactions are refused because of ML/TF each year?

**Data – quality and selection**
- Which data points are available (e.g. date, risk class, identification method, ownership structure, business model and group structure, PEP/RCA, industry, payment method, address, email, phone, legal form, occupation, source of funds/repayment capacity, product type, purpose, transaction frequency and amount, high-risk country, income, turnover and cash flow, household composition, financial commitments, recurring expenses, collateral, business plans)?
- Which are used today, how were they selected and how are they combined?
- Which information comes from external sources and which from the customer?
- Which information is approximate and which exact (quantitative/qualitative, e.g. complex ownership yes/no)?
- Is information missing in some cases, or are there data deficiencies? When was the data last updated? Is all data structured and usable?
- Is there customer information that would improve effectiveness but is missing today?

**System – limitations and adaptations**
- Are there limitations in the system you have had to work around?
- Which adaptations were made at implementation (system choices, options)?
- Are there overrides in the system?
- Have all tests been done to make the alerts show what is intended? Which tests, how often? Are they documented? What adjustments followed?

metadata.section: 1. Transaction monitoring (*Frågebatteri – validering av modellen för transaktionsmonitorering*)

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Interview question bank — 1. Transaction monitoring (*Frågebatteri – validering av modellen för transaktionsmonitorering*)
description:
**Development and evaluation**
- How are scenarios and parameters developed? Who decides and approves changes, and how are they documented (beyond the system change log)?
- How and how often are scenarios evaluated?

**Documentation**
- Is the model described and justified? Are there routines for changes? For validation?

**Alert handling**
- Who reviews, who decides? Is there segregation of duties?
- How many days between alert and decision? How often are transactions reviewed?
- Is CDD information used when reviewing alerts? How, how often? Is the relationship manager contacted? How does it work with partners/agents?
- Which other checks are made (credit reference agencies, business registers, adverse media, social media)?
- How are analysis and decisions documented, and by whom?
- Is any decision support used (additional information and risk analysis for faster decisions)?
- What difficulties do analysts experience when reviewing and reporting?

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Interview question bank — 2. Customer risk classification (derived)
description:
- What is the model meant to achieve? How do you know whether it works (target outcome, KPIs)?
- Which risk factors are used, where do the scores and weights come from, and who approved them? Which BWRA risks are deliberately not in the model, and where are they handled?
- Is the classification based on inherent risk, or are controls (enhanced monitoring, product limitations) taken into account? How?
- How are beneficial owners, representatives and associated parties included?
- What happens when data is missing (default values, exclusion, higher risk)?
- How are new customers classified before history exists?
- Who can change a customer's class manually? Is approval required? Are there other flags (e.g. extra monitoring) that act like a higher class without changing it?
- How is the class used: CDD/EDD level, review frequency, TM thresholds and scope?
- How is the distribution across classes followed up and reported? What triggers a model review?
- Where were reported customers classified before they were reported?

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Interview question bank — 3. PEP and sanctions screening (derived)
description:
- Which lists are screened, from which source, and how quickly do updates reach production? Who checks?
- Which parties and fields are screened (customers, beneficial owners, representatives, transaction parties, free text)? At onboarding, periodically, at triggers, in real time?
- How were matching thresholds set and when were they last calibrated? Is fuzzy matching configured per list?
- Which auto-discount, good-guy or whitelist rules exist? Who approves them and how are they reviewed? Is the match pair whitelisted or the customer?
- How are PEPs who have left office handled (18-month rule, de-listing)?
- How are hits investigated, by whom, how fast, with what documentation? What happens at a true hit (freeze, reject, report)?
- How is effectiveness measured (true hits, actions taken, false-hit volume)?
- Is the system a vendor product? What documentation and test results has the vendor provided?

canonical_name: Model validation report blueprint — Interview question bank — 4. BWRA as a model (derived)
description:
- How are the scores per product, customer type, channel and geography set, and from which sources?
- How are ML and TF risk distinguished?
- How are controls assessed and how is residual risk derived?
- How do results flow into CRC, TM, KYC routines and training?
- How are own suspicious activity reports and authority information used?
- What triggers an update outside the annual cycle?

Validation result scale ("traffic light"); 2. Aggregation rule ("worst result"); 3. Coverage scale for the gap analysis (Appendix 1); 4. Documentation analysis scale; 5.
