canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 3. Risk-based approach and controls
description:
**3.1 Risk-based approach**
- EN: "The risk of being used for money laundering or terrorist financing varies with variables such as customer type, countries, products and services. Situations of higher risk require more extensive measures than situations of low risk. For {{client_short}}, a risk-based approach means that the scope of measures, procedures and controls shall be continuously adapted to the risks, with the most measures applied where the risks are greatest."
- SV: "Risken att utnyttjas för penningtvätt eller finansiering av terrorism varierar beroende på variabler såsom kundtyp, länder, produkter och tjänster. Situationer med förhöjd risk kräver mer omfattande åtgärder än situationer med låg risk. För {{client_short}} innebär ett riskbaserat förhållningssätt att omfattningen av åtgärder, förfaranden och kontroller fortlöpande ska anpassas efter riskerna. Flest åtgärder ska sättas in där riskerna är störst."

**3.2 Control design responsibility**
- EN: "The compliance function shall advise on how mitigating measures can be designed. Based on the compliance function's recommendations, the head of the department concerned decides how the measures are designed."
- SV: "Compliancefunktionen ska ge råd och stöd om hur de mitigerande åtgärderna kan utformas. Chefen för berörd avdelning beslutar utifrån compliancefunktionens rekommendationer hur åtgärderna ska utformas."

**3.3 Follow-up of controls**
- EN: "The CFA shall follow up and assess how well the control measures work. The activity shall result in an assessment of residual risk in relation to the risk appetite. A high residual risk may indicate that the controls are not sufficiently effective or need to be redesigned."

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 3. Risk-based approach and controls
description: - SV: "Centralt funktionsansvarig ska följa upp och bedöma hur väl kontrollåtgärderna fungerar. Aktiviteten ska resultera i en bedömning av residualrisken i förhållande till riskaptiten. Om residualrisken är hög kan det indikera att kontrollåtgärderna inte är tillräckligt effektiva eller behöver utformas på annat sätt."

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 4. Accountability and roles
description:
**4.1 Ultimate responsibility**
- EN: "Decisions rest either on a legal mandate from the Board or the CEO, or on a delegation from either of them. The person or function holding the mandate is ultimately responsible. Ultimate responsibility can never be delegated, so there is only one ultimately responsible person or function for each task. The person or function performing a task is responsible. Responsibility can be delegated, and a task may have several responsible persons. Roles and responsibilities shall be defined and documented in mandates or job descriptions."
- SV: "Beslut grundas antingen på legalt mandat från styrelsen eller VD, eller på delegation från någon av dessa. Den person eller funktion som har legalt mandat är ytterst ansvarig. Det yttersta ansvaret kan aldrig delegeras. Det finns således alltid bara en ytterst ansvarig person eller funktion i förhållande till en uppgift. Den person eller funktion som utför en uppgift är ansvarig. Ansvar kan delegeras och det kan finnas flera ansvariga för en uppgift. Roller och ansvar ska vara definierade och dokumenterade i mandat eller arbetsbeskrivningar."

**4.2 Delegation by the SAE or CFA**
- EN: "The [SAE/CFA] may delegate responsibility and tasks to persons with adequate competence, experience and suitability, but remains ultimately responsible. Reporting to the Board and the CEO cannot be delegated."
- SV: "[SUB/CFA] kan delegera ansvar och uppgifter till personer med adekvat kompetens, erfarenhet och lämplighet men är fortfarande ytterst ansvarig. Rapporteringen till styrelse och VD kan dock inte delegeras."

**4.3 CFA independence**
- EN: "Direct reporting to the Board and the CEO ensures that the CFA holds an independent position."
- SV: "Genom direktrapportering till styrelse och VD säkerställs att centralt funktionsansvarig har en oberoende ställning."

**4.4 Veto**

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 4. Accountability and roles
description:
- EN: "The [SAE/CFA] has the authority to issue a veto whenever the [SAE/CFA] assesses that the risk of money laundering and terrorist financing is unacceptable in relation to the risk appetite adopted by the Board."
- SV: "[SUB/CFA] har befogenhet att utfärda ett veto vid alla tillfällen där denne bedömer att risken för penningtvätt och finansiering av terrorism är oacceptabel i förhållande till styrelsens beslutade riskaptit."

**4.5 Competent decision maker**
- EN: "A competent decision maker is a person with sufficient knowledge of {{client_short}}'s exposure to money laundering and terrorist financing and sufficient authority to take decisions that affect that exposure."
- SV: "Behörig beslutsfattare är en person som har tillräckliga kunskaper om verksamhetens riskexponering mot penningtvätt och finansiering av terrorism och tillräckliga befogenheter att fatta beslut som påverkar riskexponeringen."

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 5. Customer due diligence
description:
**5.1 Purpose of CDD**
- EN: "The purpose of customer due diligence is that {{client_short}} has sufficiently good knowledge of its customers and their business. This enables {{client_short}}, first, to avoid being used for money laundering and terrorist financing and, second, to act against suspected money laundering and terrorist financing."
- SV: "Syftet med kundkännedomen är att {{client_short}} ska ha tillräckligt god kännedom om sina kunder och deras affärer, så att {{client_short}} i första hand kan undvika att utnyttjas för penningtvätt och finansiering av terrorism och i andra hand kan agera mot misstänkt penningtvätt och finansiering av terrorism."

**5.2 No CDD, no relationship**
- EN: "Sufficient customer due diligence shall be obtained and documented before a business relationship is established or an occasional transaction is carried out. If sufficient customer due diligence cannot be achieved, the relationship shall not be established or maintained, and an assessment shall be made of whether to report to the FIU."
- SV: "Innan en affärsförbindelse inleds eller en enstaka transaktion utförs måste tillräcklig kundkännedom ha inhämtats och dokumenterats. Om tillräcklig kundkännedom inte kan uppnås får affärsförbindelsen inte inledas eller upprätthållas, och en bedömning ska göras av om en rapport bör lämnas till Finanspolisen."

**5.3 Escalation of simplified CDD**
- EN: "If anything during simplified measures indicates a higher risk than first assessed, more extensive measures shall be taken."
- SV: "Om något under de förenklade åtgärderna indikerar en högre risk än den ursprungliga bedömningen ska mer omfattande åtgärder vidtas."

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 6. Monitoring, investigation and reporting
description:
**6.1 Documentation standard**
- EN: "Investigations shall be carried out promptly to establish whether a suspicion exists. They shall be documented so that, when a report is made, the FIU can pursue the matter further, and so that, when an alert is closed, a reasonably informed reader clearly understands why it was closed without a report. Reports shall be made at a relatively low degree of suspicion."
- SV: "Utredningar ska ske skyndsamt i syfte att identifiera om det föreligger misstanke. Utredningen ska dokumenteras så att det vid rapportering är möjligt för Finanspolisen att utreda vidare och vid stängning så att en rimligt initierad läsare tydligt förstår varför larmet har stängts utan rapportering. Rapportering ska ske vid en relativt låg grad av misstanke."

**6.2 Customer explanation**
- EN: "The customer shall always be able to explain the purpose of the transaction and the origin of the funds and, when needed, support the explanation with evidence."
- SV: "Kunden ska alltid kunna förklara avsikten med transaktionen och varifrån medlen härrör och vid behov styrka sin förklaring med underlag."

**6.3 Refraining from execution**
- EN: "If the customer's explanation does not remove the suspicion, the transaction shall not be carried out. If refraining is not possible, or would hinder further investigation, the transaction may be carried out and reported immediately afterwards."
- SV: "Om kundens förklaring inte undanröjer misstanken får transaktionen inte genomföras. Om det inte är möjligt att avstå, eller om den vidare utredningen skulle försvåras, får transaktionen genomföras och rapporteras omedelbart i efterhand."

**6.4 Authority requests as a risk indicator**
- EN: "A request from an authority shall also be treated as a risk indicator. In addition to answering the request, the customer should be investigated, in the same way as a manual alert."

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 6. Monitoring, investigation and reporting
description:
- SV: "En myndighetsförfrågan ska även ses som en riskindikator. Utöver att besvara förfrågan bör en utredning göras av kunden. Utredningen bör hanteras i likhet med ett manuellt larm."

**6.5 Customers reported to the FIU**
- EN: "Customers reported to the FIU shall be investigated, and it shall be assessed whether continuing the relationship is within the risk appetite."
- SV: "Kunder som rapporterats till Finanspolisen ska utredas och det ska bedömas om en fortsatt kundrelation ryms inom riskaptiten."

**6.6 Alert ageing** (financial crime variant)
- EN: "An alert shall never be left unreviewed and unmanaged for more than [30] days, except for complex investigations, which are monitored by [role]."

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 7. Confidentiality, liability and protection of employees
description:
**7.1 Confidentiality**
- EN: "Employees, contractors, Board members and others taking part in the business must not disclose to the customer or any third party that a review is being carried out, that information has been passed to the AML function or that a report has been made to the FIU. The duty of confidentiality applies to each individual and carries criminal liability."
- SV: "Anställda, uppdragstagare, styrelseledamöter och andra som på liknande sätt deltar i verksamheten får inte röja för kunden eller för någon utomstående att en granskning genomförs, att uppgifter har lämnats till AML-ansvarig eller att rapportering har gjorts till Finanspolisen. Tystnadsplikten gäller för varje enskild medarbetare och är förenad med straffansvar."

**7.2 Personal liability**
- EN: "Intentionally or through gross negligence participating in money laundering or terrorist financing, neglecting the duty to scrutinise or report, or breaching confidentiality carries criminal liability. The personal liability applies to every employee."
- SV: "Att med uppsåt eller grov oaktsamhet medverka till penningtvätt eller finansiering av terrorism, åsidosätta sin gransknings- eller rapporteringsskyldighet eller bryta mot tystnadsplikten är förenat med straffansvar. Det personliga ansvaret gäller varje medarbetare."

**7.3 No reprisals**
- EN: "Employees, contractors and others taking part in the business shall not be subjected to reprisals or other adverse treatment because of their work against money laundering and terrorist financing, or because they have reported internal irregularities or non-compliance (whistleblowing)."

metadata.section: 7. Confidentiality, liability and protection of employees

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Model clauses (English and Swedish) — 7. Confidentiality, liability and protection of employees
description:
- SV: "Medarbetare, uppdragstagare eller andra som på liknande sätt deltar i verksamheten får inte utsättas för repressalier eller annan negativ särbehandling på grund av sitt arbete med att motverka penningtvätt och finansiering av terrorism eller för att de har rapporterat interna missförhållanden eller bristande regelefterlevnad (visselblåsning)."

**7.4 Source confidentiality**
- EN: "The CFA is responsible for ensuring that the identity of an employee or other source who has reported a deviation internally is not revealed and cannot be traced, and that all information gathered in an investigation remains confidential."
- SV: "CFA ansvarar för att identiteten hos en anställd eller annan källa som rapporterat ett avvikande beteende internt inte avslöjas och inte kan härledas till källan, samt för att all information som samlats in i en utredning är konfidentiell."

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Requirements-to-document matrix — Introduction
description:
Use this file to seed the requirements traceability matrix (xlsx). Each requirement area has an ID. The ID is also used in `content-mapping-by-document-type.md` and in review comments.

**How to read the level columns**
- **Policy (P):** the board's principle, decision or commitment.
- **Instruction (I):** who is responsible, the minimum standard, frequencies, decision levels and reporting.
- **Manual / routine (M):** the operational steps, evidence and system handling.
- **Elsewhere:** a mandate, a separate policy or instruction, or another deliverable.
- **"–"** means the topic does not belong at that level.

**Reference rules**
- The EU column cites Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 ("AMLD") wherever the article is certain. Uncertain articles are marked `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.
- AMLR (Regulation (EU) 2024/1624, applicable from 10 July 2027) is described by subject only. Verify article numbers before use.
- The Sweden column names the instrument and topic only. PTL = Lag (2017:630). FFFS = FFFS 2017:11. Every chapter and section number must be verified before it is written into the matrix.
- Other jurisdictions: replace the Sweden column via `{{jurisdiction}}`.

Regulatory baseline of this file: as known at 2026-10-09. Check the current versions before each use.

- **Very high risk at onboarding:**

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Roles and mandates catalogue — Introduction
description:
This catalogue lists the responsibilities, reporting points, powers and independence criteria for each role. It is drawn from the team's policy and instruction templates and from delivered instructions and mandates. Use it as the agenda for the roles workshop and as the source for section 3 of the instruction and for the mandates. Adapt every item to the client, and delete the ones that do not apply.

Terminology:
- **SAE** = specially appointed executive (*särskilt utsedd befattningshavare*, SUB). Under the AMLR, map this role to the management body member responsible for AML/CFT `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.
- **CFA** = central function officer (*centralt funktionsansvarig*). English client documents also call this role "Appointed Officer for Controlling and Reporting Obligations", "MLRO" or "AML/CFT compliance officer". Under the AMLR, map it to the compliance manager `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.

Use one label throughout a document set.

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Roles and mandates catalogue — 1. Accountability principles (put in the instruction)
description:
1. Decisions rest either on a legal mandate from the board or the CEO, or on a delegation from one of them.
2. The person or function holding the mandate is **ultimately responsible** (*ytterst ansvarig*). Ultimate responsibility can never be delegated. Each task has exactly one ultimately responsible person or function.
3. The person or function performing a task is **responsible** (*ansvarig*). Responsibility can be delegated. A task can have several responsible persons.
4. Roles and responsibilities are defined and documented in mandates or job descriptions.
5. The SAE and the CFA may delegate tasks to persons with adequate competence, experience and suitability. They remain ultimately responsible. Their **reporting to the board and the CEO cannot be delegated**.

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Roles and mandates catalogue — 2. Board of Directors (*styrelsen*)
description:
- Adopts the policy, at least annually.
- Adopts the risk appetite, including the unacceptable activities decided by the board.
- Ensures that resources are sufficient.
- Promotes a culture of sound risk management and compliance.
- Appoints the SAE and the CFA, or approves their appointment, and assesses the suitability of the CEO.
- Receives the SAE and CFA reports and follows up remediation.
- Adopts the BWRA where national rules or the client's governing documents place it with the board rather than the CEO (common for small entities and non-financial obliged entities). The BWRA is adopted by the CEO or the board, as required by national rules and the client's governing documents `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.

canonical_name: Governing documents (policies, instructions, routines) blueprint — Roles and mandates catalogue — 3. Chief Executive Officer (*VD*)
description:
- Is, under the board, ultimately responsible for the work against ML/TF.
- Proposes the SAE and the CFA and assesses their suitability. In some frameworks the CEO appoints the CFA.
- Adopts the instruction. Adopts the BWRA where national rules and the client's governing documents place it with the CEO rather than the board `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.
- Ensures sufficient resources and competence.
- Operationalises the risk appetite and establishes restrictions.
- Ensures routines for compliance with financial sanctions.
- Makes the policy available and issues detailed rules.
- Presents proposed policy changes to the board each year.
- Ensures that the CFA has adequate resources. The CFA's resource needs are evaluated continuously in a dialogue between the CFA and the CEO.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — Introduction
description:
This file holds ready-made method descriptions for the services the team most often offers. Each module gives the elements a proposal needs: purpose, steps, assessment framework, client interactions, pre-start document request, deliverables, typical exclusions and specific judgement calls. Tailor every module to the client's components. Never paste one unchanged.

Durations are indicative patterns from the team's proposals and must be confirmed per engagement. Modules marked **[draft offering]** come from internal development material and need team confirmation before use.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M1. AML/CTF model validation (TM, CRR/CRC, screening)
description:
**When.** An initial validation before a new model goes live. A periodic validation. A validation after a material change to a model, its data or the business. A validation after a supervisory or audit remark.

**Purpose text.** "The validation assesses whether the models are fit for their purpose and ensures that they meet relevant legal and functional requirements. It comprises an independent review in line with legal requirements and industry standards and is documented in a validation report describing method, assessments and results."

**Component descriptions** (one per model):

| Model | Standard description |
|---|---|
| Transaction monitoring (TM) | The system captures predefined transaction patterns and generates alerts on deviating behaviour. In addition to deviating behaviour, the model should take known ML/TF methods into account. |
| Customer risk classification (CRR/CRC) | The model assesses ML/TF risk by dividing customers into risk classes. The customer's risk class determines more extensive, in-depth and frequent controls. It may be split into natural persons and legal persons. |
| Screening (PEP/RCA and sanctions) | The model identifies PEPs, RCAs and sanctioned parties. It enables enhanced due diligence and, where relevant, stopping transactions and freezing assets. |

**The firm's method in three blocks.**

1. **Collection of documents and data.** The BWRA; model documentation; previous validation reports; an overview of the implemented TM scenarios; a review and description of supporting systems; collection of input and output data for the implemented model.
2. **Validation principles and method.** The method draws on industry guidance on AML model validation, which builds on US supervisory guidance on model risk management, and on the team's credit-risk validation experience. It has four parts:

metadata.section: M1. AML/CTF model validation (TM, CRR/CRC, screening)

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M1. AML/CTF model validation (TM, CRR/CRC, screening)
description:
- *Conceptual:* documentation, business objectives, model use, model monitoring, model selection, methodology, process for selecting risk factors, override process, governance, limitations and assumptions, data.
   - *Implementation risk:* test plan and testing, data, change management.
   - *Input risk:* data, missing values.
   - *Output risk:* sensitivity, model effectiveness, quantitative and qualitative validation.
3. **Assessment areas.** The 12-row table in `template.md`, Table 3.

**The validation in structured steps (proposal bullets).**

- Review internal documents, routines and model documentation.
- Check that the scenarios, parameters, thresholds and risk factors applied are appropriate and relevant.
- Evaluate the model's effectiveness.
- Test the data used by the models to ensure that it is complete and accurate.
- Assess the link to the BWRA and the roles and responsibilities for model management in internal rules.
- Hold working meetings to fact-check and agree on preliminary observations. These are joint workshops for status follow-up and reporting.
- End with written validation reports.

**Five-stage validation process** (for the method appendix or the service presentation):

| Stage | Content |
|---|---|
| 1. Planning | Set the validation scope, objectives, timeline and approach |
| 2. Discovery | Identify, request and organise information. Discuss with downstream model users. Prepare tools and quantitative code. Review previous validation reports and findings. |
| 3. Analysis and validation | Compare model methodology, data and performance with requirements and benchmarks. Quantitative validation. Qualitative validation. |

metadata.section: M1. AML/CTF model validation (TM, CRR/CRC, screening)

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M1. AML/CTF model validation (TM, CRR/CRC, screening)
description:
| Stage | Content |
|---|---|
| 4. Findings and reporting | Convert test outcomes into findings. Aggregate findings. Report or present at the risk forum or committee. A clear fact check before the report, with a walkthrough of observations and recommendations. Observations can be reported iteratively. |
| 5. Follow-up | Follow up on actions taken on the findings |

**Plan pattern.**

- Before start: documentation request; initial review; optional introductory meeting.
- Phase 1, preliminary assessment: governance and conceptual soundness per model, with preliminary reports on conceptual design, data, model use and, for TM only, model performance.
- Phase 2, final assessment, including model effectiveness where in scope.
- Phase 3, delivery: the validation report and a clarification meeting.

**Deliverables.** One validation report per model in Word or PDF. It contains the method, the review walkthrough, the results of the review with explanations and recommendations for improvement. A presentation of the validation results. The grading scale comes from `model-validation-report`.

**Contact model.** One main contact at the client who coordinates with the compliance function (*centralt funktionsansvarig* or the compliance officer), the specially appointed executive (*särskilt utsedd befattningshavare*, SUB), the AML officer, the model owner, the IT model owner and the vendor contact.

**Typical exclusions.**

- A conceptual review only for models not yet in production. Output and effectiveness are not assessed.
- No mapping against the BWRA or the AML Act where the time frame does not allow it.
- No mapping against specific guidelines, e.g. on restrictive measures, for screening.
- Collecting information missing from the submitted material is billed separately.

**Judgement calls.**

- **Prerequisites.** A successful validation needs five things in place:

metadata.section: M1. AML/CTF model validation (TM, CRR/CRC, screening)

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M1. AML/CTF model validation (TM, CRR/CRC, screening)
description:
- a model risk or governance framework with a model inventory
  - a validation framework
  - model documentation
  - a named model owner
  - a validation function that is independent of model owners and developers

  First-time validations often lack these. Offer the prerequisites first, using the `model-documentation` blueprint for the documentation, and keep the validation team separate.
- **Shared systems.** Some entities use a system owned by a parent, partner bank or vendor. Mark the parts where the system owner is responsible and the client must ensure follow-up. Assessment points that can be performed jointly for several entities are offered as coordinated parts, priced per entity with and without coordination.
- **Delivery model.** One-off validation, or continuous validation as a service (VaaS). The case for VaaS rests on five points:
  - independence from the first line
  - alignment with industry practice
  - reduced key-person risk
  - long-term cost efficiency
  - resource efficiency, because the client can let the service cover all or part of the model portfolio
- **AI assistance.** If parts of the validation are AI-assisted, say so in the assumptions.

**Pre-start document request.** BWRA; model documentation for each model; previous validation reports and follow-up of findings; overview of implemented scenarios and thresholds (TM); risk factors and weights (CRR); list sources, matching and fuzzy-logic settings (screening); system description and data lineage; input and output data extracts; model governance documents (model risk policy, validation instruction); change log since the last validation.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M2. Business-wide risk assessment (BWRA, *allmän riskbedömning*)
description:
**Overview: three pillars.**

1. **Inherent risk.** The starting point is typology-based. The typology-based approach is fuelled by data to determine exposure, enable trend analysis and align with regulatory expectations.
2. **Controls and mitigating actions.** Assessed through targeted questionnaires. Controls are divided into general and specific controls; the specific controls are tied to specific risk factors.
3. **Residual risk.** The ML/TF risk that remains after controls and mitigating actions. Findings and impacts are documented and used as the basis for action plans.

**Nine steps.**

| # | Step | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Define the inherent risk factors and typologies | Use external and internal sources. The risk factors and typologies are described and analysed in the report. Risk categories: products and services, customers, geography, distribution channels, other qualitative risk factors. |
| 2 | Weight the inherent risk factors | Factors and typologies are weighted within their risk category, as per the methodology, and defined individually for each risk type |
| 3 | Analyse exposure | Data is collected and reviewed and used as a factor to determine the exposure |
| 4 | Assess inherent risk | Steps 1–3 give the inherent risk. A mix of qualitative and quantitative approaches is recommended. A separate score is given for each risk type. |
| 5 | Define control effectiveness categories | As per the methodology |
| 6 | Identify general and specific controls | General controls show the overall control environment. Specific controls are tied to risk factors. |
| 7 | Assess control effectiveness | Through a targeted control questionnaire, on (i) effectiveness and (ii) design and documentation. Shortcomings are documented for each control. A separate score is given for each risk type. |

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M2. Business-wide risk assessment (BWRA, *allmän riskbedömning*)
description:
| # | Step | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | Derive residual risk | Inherent risk combined with controls gives residual risk. A separate score is given for each risk type. Document clearly how findings affect the assessment. |
| 9 | Draw up the action plan | Based on residual risk and control deficiencies: what, by whom and by when |

**Offer options.** A gap analysis of the current risk assessment and methodology. Defining a BWRA methodology suited to the business. Carrying out the BWRA, with the option to include other risk types such as sanctions. Project management of the BWRA. General support.

**Client interactions.** A data request covering volumes per product, customer segment, geography and channel; a control questionnaire; workshops with first and second line; a validation meeting on preliminary results; board presentation.

**Link.** Delivery follows `aml-ctf-risk-assessment`.

---

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M3. AMLR readiness, maturity assessment or FCP discovery
description:
**Positioning.** A low-investment alternative to a traditional maturity assessment. It addresses the challenge of securing budget before the client knows its AMLR gaps or the investments needed. The results become the base for investment planning.

**Framework domains.** The firm's FCP framework is built on supervisory expectations, EBA guidelines, AMLR requirements and best-practice FCP operating models. It is tailored to industry and size.

1. Oversight and control, including training and awareness
2. Business intelligence, reporting and effectiveness
3. FCP strategy and risk foundations
4. FCP analytics and intelligence, including model validation
5. FCP prevention and customer lifecycle controls
6. FCP operations
7. Data, technology and enablers

**Approach.**

| Step | What | Duration | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | A tailored digital questionnaire aligned with the framework | ~2 weeks | Identify immediate gaps, areas with a high likelihood of non-compliance, inefficiencies and risk concentrations, and needs for supporting evidence. Minimises consultant hours while capturing a broad, structured overview. |
| B | Validation workshops (one to three sessions) with Compliance, FCP, Risk, Operations and IT | ~1 week | Validate assumptions. Clarify context and constraints. Understand processes "in reality". Assess risk appetite, ambition and transformation needs. |
| C | AMLR readiness report and roadmap | ~1 week | Gaps, strategic recommendations and a clear, defensible, risk-based plan to reach AMLR compliance while strengthening the operating model |

metadata.section: M3. AMLR readiness, maturity assessment or FCP discovery

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M3. AMLR readiness, maturity assessment or FCP discovery
description:
**Maturity score.** The readiness report gives a maturity score per framework domain and overall. Use the readiness scale in `gap-analysis/references/rating-scales.md` section 6 (Advanced / Progressing / Early Stage / Not Started, with the share of requirements implemented) and state the scale in the proposal. Gaps found in the discovery are rated on the 5-level deficiency scale in section 1 of the same file, so that a later gap analysis continues on the same scale.

**Value statements.**

- A clear view of current AMLR readiness
- Prioritised risk areas
- Recommendations and strategic direction
- A pragmatic, risk-based roadmap including the high-level investment need
- An impact assessment if identified risks remain unaddressed
- Evidence-based decision material for internal investment discussions
- Decision-makers on the same page

**Background content: the domains most affected by AMLR.**

| Domain | What changes |
|---|---|
| Risk assessment and methodology | Stronger quantification and evidence |
| KYC/CDD | Deeper verification and EU-wide consistency |
| Transaction monitoring | Model governance, scenario calibration, data quality |
| Governance and accountability | Clear roles, documentation, oversight |
| Outsourcing | Stricter control expectations and due diligence |
| Reporting | Wider scope on specific data attributes, which needs strong data management |

Verify each claim against the final AMLR text and Level 2 measures `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`.

**Team model.** A core team with a mix of seniority (engagement lead and AML/CTF expert, AMLR expert, AML/CTF expert). An expert panel for oversight, strategic guidance and quality assurance. An extended expert panel of financial law, data management and technology and infrastructure experts, called in as needed. Price model: fixed price.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M4. Pre-study, target operating model and roadmap (transformation)
description:
**Positioning.** A short, time-boxed, fixed-price pre-study with low risk for the client. It serves as the entry point to execution. It combines qualitative work (interviews, workshops, questionnaires) with quantitative work (desk research and data). The final report gives a maturity score (on the readiness scale in `gap-analysis/references/rating-scales.md` section 6), the gaps to the target state and a transformation strategy with an actionable roadmap.

**Five phases.**

| Phase | Purpose and objective | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Mobilisation | Alignment and a robust foundation through stakeholder consensus, defined roles and governance | Confirm scope, business objectives, guiding principles and prioritisation; agree governance and the FCP framework to use |
| 2. AMLR impact and target state | Understand AMLR impact and the client's risk exposure as input to the target operating model | Translate AMLR into requirements; consolidate available risk assessments; design the target state with all three lines of defence |
| 3. Maturity assessment | Assess current practice against the target state | Frameworks, policies, governance, technology, data, organisation, products and geographic risk; benchmark against regulatory expectations and industry standards |
| 4. Gap-closure initiatives | Define practical initiatives to close the gaps | Actionable initiatives aligned with requirements and the target state |
| 5. Risk-based roadmap and final report | A prioritised roadmap | Balances risk, priorities, resources and regulatory urgency |

Expected results: a clear picture of current workflows and systems, duplicated processes and bottlenecks, and recommendations for data management and collaboration. Next steps: present the mapping; plan a proof of concept; evaluate savings and return on investment.

Formats: standard (2–4 weeks, light mapping, workshop-driven) or enhanced (8–10 weeks, deeper data model, vendor insight and regulatory overlay).

**Typical exclusions.** Implementation, architecture design, vendor contracting.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M5. Sanctions: implementing the guidelines on restrictive measures
description:
**The five areas of the guidelines** (EBA/GL/2024/14 and EBA/GL/2024/15) `[VERIFY REFERENCE: scope and application date]`:

1. Governance and allocation of responsibilities
2. Exposure assessment of sanctions risk
3. KYC and screening
4. Transaction monitoring and transaction screening
5. Reporting and handling of frozen assets

**Offer elements.** Risk assessment; gap analysis against the new guidelines; implementation or optimisation of screening systems; processes for managing sanctions risk; governing documents; training.

**AMLR link.** Under the AMLR, targeted financial sanctions become part of the AML framework: the internal policies, the risk assessment, customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring. Present sanctions as integrated with AML work, not as a separate silo `[VERIFY REFERENCE: AMLR articles]`.

**Next steps block** (for the end of the proposal or pitch).

- **Scope and time.** The branch or the whole bank? What ambition level, and when must everything be done? Project planning. A project structure and steering group, if needed.
- **Secure resources.** Ensure competence and capacity, which often compete with daily operations.
- **Start the work.** Actions are taken according to plan.
- **External needs.** What can the client do with its own competence and resources? What external help is needed? What is the budget?

**Prioritisation statement.** Some measures should be in place by the application date, for example the exposure assessment, organisation and basic governance. More technical parts, such as list management and model documentation, should have started, with a clear plan for completion.

**Link.** `sanctions-risk-assessment`.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M7. Managed services (AML/CTF as a service)
description:
**Modules.**

1. **AML/CTF framework.** At least annual review and continuous adaptation of the following, plus model validation of CRR and TM:
   - the BWRA
   - policies, guidelines and routines
   - the CRR model
   - the KYC questionnaire, including answer options
   - TM scenarios, including model documentation
   - internal reporting of KPIs and KRIs
2. **Operational functions.** The service is system-agnostic. It covers:
   - KYC analysis, including CDD, EDD and ODD responses, and handling of PEP/RCA screening
   - TM alert review and investigations
   - reporting to the financial intelligence unit
   - sanctions screening hit review and investigations
3. **Internal control: outsourced or co-sourced MLRO or compliance function.** This covers:
   - regulatory monitoring and support with implementing changes
   - reporting to the compliance function and management
   - control of AML/CTF processes
   - continuous follow-up of deficiencies and measures taken
   - AML/CTF training of employees, at least annually

**Proposal specifics.** Service scope per module; volume and capacity assumptions; service levels; reporting; start-up and knowledge transfer; governance meetings; notice period; a recurring price model.

**Outsourcing.** The client keeps responsibility for compliance. Outsourcing rules apply, including the EBA outsourcing guidelines and any national notification duty `[VERIFY REFERENCE]`. State this in the assumptions.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Method modules for proposals — M8. Second opinion or expert review
description:
**Purpose.** A focused, rapid assessment by senior experts to validate strengths, identify blind spots and find improvements, without committing to a full audit or transformation. It is collaborative and solution-oriented. A formal review with ratings follows `compliance-review-report` instead.

**Steps.**

1. Discovery and scoping, with review boundaries and success criteria
2. Documentation analysis: configurations, policies, workflows and metrics
3. Stakeholder interviews
4. Comparative assessment against relevant industry standards
5. Opportunity mapping, prioritised by impact, feasibility and regulatory relevance
6. A strategic insight workshop

**Typical focus areas.** TM rule logic, thresholds and alert quality; screening match quality and false positives; AI/ML model governance and explainability; CDD/KYC process and data use; AMLR gaps and supervisory preparation; vendor implementations.

**Variant: mock supervisory review.** Consultants with experience from a supervisory authority perform a review modelled on a supervisory inspection.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Pricing structure for proposals — Introduction
description: This file describes **structure only**. It contains no hourly rates, rate tiers, price levels, cost figures, margins or discount rules, and none may be added. Actual figures come from the firm's internal pricing tool, after internal approval, and reach the assistant only through the `pricing:` block of the proposal brief.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Pricing structure for proposals — 1. Division of responsibility
description:
| Who | Does what |
|---|---|
| Deal owner or engagement lead | Scopes and estimates hours per component, runs the pricing tool and proposes the price model |
| The firm's approval chain | Approves the price before it is sent. The roles are listed in the internal tool and typically run from deal owner and team manager through head of business area and head of sales to CEO for larger deviations. |

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Pricing structure for proposals — 2. Price models
description:
| Model | Swedish | When it fits | What the proposal must state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed price for the project | *Fast pris* | Well-defined scope, standard method, known content and environment | Total excluding VAT; the deliverables it covers; the invoicing trigger (e.g. "invoiced after the final report(s) and presentation"); what is billed separately; how scope changes are handled |
| Time and material with an estimate | *Löpande räkning* | Scope depends on findings; uncertain data quality | Estimated hours per component; role split; rates as supplied in the brief; estimated total ("approximately"); that actual time is billed; how consumption is reported |
| Per-entity or per-unit price | *Pris per bolag/enhet* | Several similar entities, e.g. group companies or banks sharing one system | Price per entity, with and without coordinated parts |
| Recurring fee | *Löpande avgift* | Managed services, validation as a service, outsourced functions | Service scope; capacity (% of an FTE) or volume assumptions; period; indexation; notice period; start-up phase |
| Framework agreement call-off | *Avrop* | An agreement is in place | The agreement reference; rates follow the agreement |
| Phased offer | *Etappvis* | Pre-study or discovery followed by implementation | A fixed price for phase 1; later phases decided on its results |

Choose by asking two questions:

1. Can the scope be fixed before we start?
   - Yes: fixed price.
   - No: time and material with an estimate, or a phased offer.
2. Is the service recurring?
   - Yes: a recurring fee based on capacity or volumes.

A framework agreement overrides both answers: follow the agreement.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Pricing structure for proposals — 4. Fixed-price risk questions
description:
Answer the five questions before offering a fixed price:

1. To what extent do standard methods exist for this work?
2. How well does the firm know the content?
3. How well does the firm know the client's environment?
4. How much must the firm rely on the client to deliver on time and on budget?
5. How confident is the firm in the scoping, including time and resource allocation?

The tool translates the answers into a recommended risk buffer, which is added to the fee. The rating scale is `[TO CONFIRM]`. Weak answers on questions 3–5 are a reason to choose a phased offer or time and material.

- The basis: hours per component and role mix (for T&M and as context for a fixed price)
- What the price covers (link to the deliverables)
- What is billed separately, e.g. "collection of information missing from the submitted material is not included and is billed as additional hourly fees", travel and other expenses
- The invoicing trigger, e.g. "invoiced after the final report(s) and presentation" for a fixed price, or periodic invoicing of actual hours for T&M `[TO CONFIRM: firm standard]`
- The calendar basis where weekly cost is shown: "a working day of 8 hours and a working week of 40 hours"
- Offer validity, given as a date

**Only if the brief supplies it and firm practice is to show it:**

- Rates per role
- Hours per person

**Never:**

- Rate card tiers, internal cost, margins or contribution figures
- Discount reasoning or approval comments
- Comparisons with the client's earlier prices

metadata.section: 5. What goes into the client-facing price section

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Pricing structure for proposals — 6. Consistency checks before sending
description:
1. Hours per component add up to the total hours.
2. Role shares add up to 100 %, and role hours equal total hours × share.
3. Role hours × rates equal the stated T&M estimate, within rounding.
4. Price, hours and team are identical in the summary, price section and appendices.
5. Only one price model is present, unless options are deliberately labelled.
6. The currency follows the client country, and VAT is stated.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Pricing structure for proposals — 6.1 Seniority ladder
description: 1st-year Associate → Associate → Senior Associate → Manager → Senior Manager → Director → Managing Director.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Pricing structure for proposals — 6.2 Mapping to RFP price-sheet categories
description:
Client price sheets often use other categories. Suggested mapping, to be confirmed per firm `[TO CONFIRM]`:

| RFP category | Firm seniority |
|---|---|
| Partner | Managing Director / Director |
| Senior Manager | Senior Manager |
| Manager | Manager |
| Senior Consultant | Senior Associate |
| Consultant | Associate |
| Junior Consultant | 1st-year Associate |

Give one rate per category in the client's sheet. Note any deviations, for example for remote, on-site or other resource locations, in the description column the client provides.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Proposal inputs: brief extension and profile fields — 2. Proposal brief block
description:
Paste this under the request context and fill in what is known.

```yaml
proposal:
  type: new | follow-on | rfp-response | framework-call-off
  format: word | pptx-full | pptx-short | pptx-discovery | rfp-native
  engagement_title: "Validation of AML models"
  need: >                              # required. The client's need in one to three sentences, as the client stated it
    ...
  trigger: "new CRR model goes live in Q2" # required. Supervisory finding | new model | AMLR | audit | growth | other
  deadline_driver: "2027-07-10 AMLR application"   # optional
  components:                          # required. One entry per separately estimated part
    - name: "Transaction monitoring model"
      status: in-production | planned-go-live | last-validated-YYYY
      notes: "vendor system"
  exclusions: ["no mapping against guideline X"]   # known exclusions or client wishes
  client_wishes: ["report in Swedish", "presentation to the board"]
  start: "2026-11"
  end: "2027-01"
  decision_date: "2026-10-30"
  valid_until: "2026-11-30"            # date. Never invent; use the profile standard if the user says so
  pricing:                             # figures from the firm's pricing tool, after approval
    model: fixed | time-and-material | per-entity | recurring | framework | phased
    total_excl_vat: "[from pricing tool]"
    currency: SEK

    role_split: {"QA/Director": "~10%", "Execution/Associate": "~90%"}

    invoicing: "after final report and presentation"
    billed_separately: ["collection of missing information", "travel"]
    approved: yes | no
  rfp:
    documents: ["RFP.pdf", "Annex 1 requirements.xlsx"]
```

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Responding to an RFP or procurement questionnaire
description: Reference catalogue `references/rfp-response.md` of the FCP blueprint `proposal` (skill fcp-bp-proposal). Sections: 1. What an incoming RFP usually contains; 2. RFP response process; 3. Compliance matrix; 4. Evaluation criteria and where to answer them; 5. Supplier questionnaire: question categories and where the answers come from; 6. Rules for RFP answers

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Responding to an RFP or procurement questionnaire — 1. What an incoming RFP usually contains
description:
The team's examples show the structure clients use. Map each part to an action.

| RFP part | What to do |
|---|---|
| Introduction to the client | Read for context and use in Background. Do not copy it back. |
| Purpose and objectives | Restate them in "Identified needs" and in the summary |
| The assignment (often with an annex: assignment description, requirements and delivery) | Build the compliance matrix from it, line by line |
| Timetable: dispatch, first answer, presentation, final offer, start | Log every date. Plan internal review before the first deadline. |
| Tender instructions and legal requirements, e.g. registration for VAT and tax, mandatory content of the answer, electronic submission | Confirm each requirement explicitly ("Fulfilled: yes") |
| Binding period of the offer, and price validity on extension, possibly with indexation | State it in the price section and contacts |
| Evaluation criteria | Mirror them in the structure (section 4 below) |
| Confidentiality and the client's right to use the material | Note it. A confidentiality undertaking may be needed before asking questions. |
| Questions and answers (in writing; may be shared with all bidders) | Send questions before the deadline. Avoid revealing our approach in questions. |
| Contacts and annexes (requirements, sustainability questionnaire, price sheet, framework agreement) | Answer every annex in its own format |

**Phased RFPs.** Some RFPs describe phases themselves, for example phase I define, phase II build and phase III implement. They also set competence requirements for the team, such as a senior project leader, ERM, compliance, internal control and change management. Answer phase by phase. Show a team table that ticks each required competence against a named person.

metadata.section: 1. What an incoming RFP usually contains

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Responding to an RFP or procurement questionnaire — 2. RFP response process
description:
These steps are added to the proposal method's steps 1–10.

1. Confirm receipt and, if asked, the intention to tender. Log every deadline: questions, submission, presentation and the binding period of the offer.
2. Build the compliance matrix (section 3) for every requirement and question, in the client's numbering.
3. Ask clarifying questions in writing before the question deadline. Assume that answers may be shared with all bidders.
4. Answer in the client's structure and order, even if it differs from ours. Confirm every mandatory requirement explicitly.
5. Mirror the evaluation criteria (section 4) in the summary and in the method, team and quality assurance sections.
6. Fill the supplier questionnaire from the profile (section 5).
7. Propose any deviations from the client's framework agreement in tracked changes, with a reason.
8. Map our seniority ladder to the client's price-sheet categories (`pricing-structure.md`, section 6.2).
9. Run the internal review and price approval. Submit before the deadline in the required channel, and keep proof of submission.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Responding to an RFP or procurement questionnaire — 3. Compliance matrix
description:
One row per requirement or question, in the client's numbering. Deliver it as an Excel sheet or as a table in an appendix.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Ref. | The client's number, e.g. 2.3 or Q17 |
| Section | The client's section or group |
| Requirement or question | Quoted or summarised |
| Type | Mandatory / desirable / information |
| Compliance | Yes / partly / no / not applicable |
| Answer | The answer text, or a short answer with a reference |
| Where in our proposal | Section, page or appendix |
| Evidence attached | File name |
| Owner (internal) | Who answers |
| Status (internal) | Draft / reviewed / final |

Remove the internal columns before submission unless the client asks for them.

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Responding to an RFP or procurement questionnaire — 4. Evaluation criteria and where to answer them
description:
The criteria seen in the team's examples, and where the proposal should earn the points:

| Criterion | Where to score |
|---|---|
| Commitment and engagement | Summary; understanding of needs; tailored method |
| Availability | Plan; team allocation (% of time); start date; named substitutes |
| Competence and presentation | Team table; CVs; experience section; the presentation meeting |
| Industry experience | References; experience lines in the CVs; segment-specific method details |
| Quality assurance and independence | Named QA role; review process; independence statement; conflict check |
| Fee | Price section: clear model, reconciled figures, no hidden extras |
| Organisation of the work | Contact model; governance; phase plan; client time needed |

metadata.section: 5. Supplier questionnaire: question categories and where the answers come from

canonical_name: Proposal and RFP response blueprint — Responding to an RFP or procurement questionnaire — 6. Rules for RFP answers
description:
1. Answer every question, even with "not applicable" plus a reason. An empty cell scores zero.
2. Keep the client's numbering and order. Never answer "see attached" without a page or section reference.
3. Confirm mandatory requirements with an explicit yes or no and one sentence.
4. Do not change the client's templates or price sheets. Add notes in the fields provided.
5. Use the client's terminology in answers. Keep our method names secondary.
6. Use firm facts only from the profile, with an as-of date that is still valid.
7. Name references only with recorded consent. Otherwise describe the client type.
8. Submit before the deadline, in the required channel and format. Keep proof of submission.

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — Claims and messaging
description: Reference catalogue `references/claims-and-messaging.md` of the FCP blueprint `firm-and-team-presentation` (skill fcp-bp-firm-and-team-presentation). Sections: 1. Messaging building blocks; 2. Substantiation rules; 3. Weak and strong; 4. Residue and leakage check (before sending)

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — Claims and messaging — 1. Messaging building blocks
description:
These are the messages the team's material uses repeatedly, neutralised. Use them when the profile supports them. Each needs a proof point from the profile or the brief.

| Message | Typical wording | Proof point to pair it with |
|---|---|---|
| Expertise mix | "We combine regulatory and legal expertise with strategic, operational, technical and transformation capabilities." | The team composition; backgrounds in `facts.fcp_team_backgrounds` |
| Practitioners | "Many of our consultants come from operational first-line positions in banks and other financial institutions, so we understand the practical side of AML work." | Expert background lines |
| Supervisory insight | "Experience from supervisory authorities and financial intelligence units." | Only if people in the profile have such backgrounds |
| Full lifecycle | "Supporting our clients in every step, from analysis and advice to implementation and operations." | Service lines |
| Proportionate | "Tailored to your industry and size, ensuring a proportionate response." | Segment variants of the method |
| System-agnostic | "We do not depend on the specific systems you use." | Managed services delivery model |
| Integrated FCP | "Fraud and corruption are managed as an integrated part of financial crime prevention, with efficiency gains from coordination with AML." | Combined risk assessment method |
| Low threshold | "A structured yet low-cost discovery phase, which gives decision material before investment." | Discovery offer with duration |
| Trusted adviser | "We seek to be a trusted adviser and find business-oriented solutions that fit your operating model, with a high focus on compliance." | References |

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — Claims and messaging — 2. Substantiation rules
description:
| Claim type | Allowed source | If no source |
|---|---|---|
| Firm size, offices, founding year, client count | `facts.*` with a valid `as_of` | Omit the number |
| "Leading", "largest", "most specialised", "unmatched" | `approved_claims` with substantiation | Rephrase descriptively, e.g. "a team of [N] FCP specialists" |
| Years of experience | `people[].aml_experience_since` | Omit |
| "Our experts wrote / drafted…" | `people[].highlights` that say exactly that | Omit |
| Market and crime statistics | A primary external source with year | `[DATA NEEDED: source]`; never invent |
| Results of earlier engagements | `references[]` outcomes, with consent | A qualitative description of the client type |
| AI or automation benefits ("x % faster") | Measured firm results in the profile, or a cited study | A qualitative benefit only |
| Quotes and testimonials | Profile, with attribution and consent | No quote |
| Regulatory dates and requirements | The official text, verified | `[VERIFY REFERENCE]` |

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — Claims and messaging — 3. Weak and strong
description:
| Weak | Strong |
|---|---|
| "Confused by regulations? Our experts wrote the rules themselves." | "Team members have taken part in drafting national AML legislation and in international standard-setting work." (If the profile confirms it.) |
| "The most specialised AML consultants on the market." | "A team of [N] specialists in AML and financial crime prevention, with backgrounds from banks, supervisors and financial intelligence units." |
| "Legacy systems? Not AMLR compliant." | "Batch monitoring and manual onboarding will be hard to reconcile with the AMLR's expectations on monitoring and data. Here is what typically needs to change." |
| "Fraud is growing by a third every year." (no source) | "[Figure] increase in reported fraud, [year] ([source])." |
| "Head of Financial Crime at a Nordic tier-1 bank: 'The workshop transformed our approach.'" (no record) | No quote, or a consented quote from the profile |
| "AMLR applies from June 2027." | "The AMLR applies from 10 July 2027." |

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — Claims and messaging — 4. Residue and leakage check (before sending)
description:
- Search the deck, notes and file properties for every name in `identity.former_names`.
- Search for every client name used in decks that this deck was copied from.
- Remove internal slides: growth ambitions, revenue models, target client lists, go-to-market notes, "notes to self".
- Remove draft comments in any language, lorem ipsum, "X & X" and empty template slides.
- Check that the language is consistent, including headings carried over from another country's version.

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats
description: Reference catalogue `references/one-pager-and-cv-formats.md` of the FCP blueprint `firm-and-team-presentation` (skill fcp-bp-firm-and-team-presentation). Sections: Introduction; A1. "What's new" four-box one-pager; A2. A4 service brochure (two to four panels); A3. Team one-pager; A4. Offering one-pager (template); A5. Workshop invitation; B1. Long CV (one page per person, the firm format); B2. Short CV block (for pitch decks, three per slide); B3. Expert background line (team slide); B4. Team structure slide (larger pitches); C. Reference case card

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — Introduction
description:
All formats take firm facts, people and references from the profile (`profile-fields.md`). Write in `{{language}}` and use the visual profile.

---

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — A1. "What's new" four-box one-pager
description:
The team uses this as a teaser before or after meetings. It is one slide or one page with four boxes, refreshed every quarter or whenever something material changes.

| Box | Heading (sv / en) | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | *Vad är nytt?* / What's new? | Two or three recent developments: new guidelines, supervisory decisions, changes in supervisory practice. Each item has its source and date. |
| 2 | *Våra rekommendationer* / Our recommendations | Two or three concrete actions. Examples: review whether model validation is truly independent and good enough to catch input data errors; adapt TM scenarios to the BWRA; consider combining AML, fraud and cyber in one financial crime organisation. |
| 3 | *Vad gör andra?* / What are others doing? | Anonymised market observations. Examples: banks implementing annual validations; defining AML risk appetite with KPIs against risk tolerance; reviewing fraud operating models. No client names. |
| 4 | *Vårt erbjudande* / Our offer | Two or three services with a one-line benefit each, from the profile, e.g. outsourced TM alert handling, validation as a service, a mock supervisory review |

**Rules.** No supervisory decision about a named institution unless it is public and relevant, and even then refer to the decision, not to the institution's failings. Date the one-pager.

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — A2. A4 service brochure (two to four panels)
description:
1. **Cover:** service name and a list of service types, e.g. advisory · gap analyses · targeted reviews · ongoing support · training.
2. **Why it matters:** the risk narrative in two short paragraphs; typologies; links to other financial crime; one or two sourced facts.
3. **How we help:** four blocks, each with three to five bullets: risk assessment; gap analysis; advisory and ongoing support; training.
4. **About us and contact:** `boilerplate.about_long`, the FCP team positioning, one or two contacts, the website.

metadata.section: A2. A4 service brochure (two to four panels)

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — A3. Team one-pager
description:
- **Heading:** "Effective anti-money laundering and financial crime prevention"
- **Centre:** an AML service wheel with six areas, e.g. governance and frameworks; risk models; effectiveness; reviews and validations; gap analysis; data and analytics.
- **Side columns**, each with four or five "why it matters" bullets and a link to AML: ABC; fraud prevention; sanctions compliance.
- **Footer:** contact.

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — A4. Offering one-pager (template)
description:
| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| Offering name | [Service name] |
| Short description | Two or three sentences: what it is and the point of view |
| Pain points and trend | Three bullets: the client situation that triggers the need |
| Our offer | Modules or steps, with duration where relevant |
| Client value | Three to five outcome bullets |
| Entry offer | Low-threshold first step |
| Contact | One or two people |

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — A5. Workshop invitation
description:
| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| Title | "[Topic] workshop: let's explore [topic] together" |
| Lead | Who it is for; format (e.g. two hours, free of charge, collaborative); the participants we suggest (compliance, technology, business) |
| What you can expect | Insights and inspiration (findings from our market survey or experience); a tailored dialogue on where you are; identifying opportunities; concrete takeaways (two or three action points); pathways forward (possible follow-ups) |
| Why join | It is not a generic tech pitch. It is a pragmatic, insight-driven session. If you have a specific area in mind, we will focus on it. |
| Practical | Date options, location, contact |

---

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — B1. Long CV (one page per person, the firm format)
description:
| Block | Content |
|---|---|
| Header | Name; title; three to five core competence tags; email; phone |
| Education and certifications | Degree, institution, years; certifications |
| Core competences | Three to six tags (may repeat the header) |
| Industry experience | Four to six headed paragraphs: "**[Assignment or role type]:** what was done, scale and result". Most relevant first. |
| Positions prior to {{firm_name}} | Employer, role, years, one-line scope. Employer names as approved by the person. |
| Languages | Language and level (native, fluent, working, basic) |

**Rules**

- Write consistently in the third person. Do not switch between "I" and the person's name.
- Describe client assignments by client type (e.g. "a Swedish credit market company"), not by client name, unless consent is recorded.
- The title must match the team slide and the profile.
- Tailor the order of the industry-experience paragraphs to the engagement or topic.
- Remove outdated "will join" statements, placeholder phone numbers and similar.

metadata.section: B1. Long CV (one page per person, the firm format)

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — One-pager, invitation, CV and reference formats — B2. Short CV block (for pitch decks, three per slide)
description:
"[Name] is a [title] specialising in [practice]. [He or she or they] hold[s] [degree] from [institution]. [One sentence on background]."

- **Leadership and key projects:** three to five bullets: "[Role or assignment type]: [what and result]"
- **Key skills and competences:** five to seven items
- Contact line: title, phone, email

Group the slides by competence, for example "Regulatory and compliance experts", "Model validation and FCP process experts", "Technology, innovation and FCP transformation experts".

description:
| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Client | Descriptor (e.g. "Nordic tier-1 bank", "Global fintech company"). The real name only if `consent_to_name` is true. |
| Engagement | Title, e.g. "FCP transformation programme" |

canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — Firm profile: content fields (master list) — Introduction
description:
Facts about the issuing firm do not belong in blueprints. They belong in the **firm profile**, a file in the firm profile supplied with the request, named in `issuing_firm.profile`. This file defines the **content fields** the profile must hold so that presentations and proposals can be produced without inventing facts. The profile also holds the visual identity fields that `_core/output-formats.md` relies on.

**Rules for the profile**

- Every fact that can change carries an `as_of` date.
- Every positioning claim carries its substantiation and an owner.
- Personal data is included only for people who have agreed to be presented. CVs are marked `publishable`.
- Client names appear only in the internal `client_name` field of references and are shown only when `consent_to_name` is true and has not expired.
- Rates, cost, margins and discount rules are **never** part of the profile.

**Field status**

- **R** = required by any presentation or proposal that mentions the firm.
- **C** = required for the element that uses it, such as a CV pack or reference slide.
- **O** = optional.

description: This file shows how the team presents its financial crime prevention services. canonical_name: Firm and team presentation blueprint — FCP service catalogue: structure and standard descriptions — 1. Service architecture
description:
The team presents its offering in two main blocks, with transformation and training as cross-cutting capabilities.

| Block | What it is | Typical services |
|---|---|---|
| **Advisory** (*rådgivning*) | Specialist projects and interim support | AML and FCP advisory; AML and FCP transformation; preparation for supervisory inspections; KYC/ODD/EDD; transaction monitoring; model validation; risk assessment; anti-bribery and corruption; FCP operating model; fraud management; governance framework; screening (sanctions, PEP, adverse media) |
| **Managed services** (*förvaltade tjänster, outsourcing*) | Ongoing operation of parts of the client's FCP work | AML/CTF framework maintenance; operational functions (KYC, ODD, EDD, alerts in transaction monitoring, data and analytics in AML, risk measurement); internal control (independent audit, co-sourcing of the MLRO function) |
| **Transformation and technology** | Strategy-to-execution change, platforms, automation | Pre-study and target operating model; implementation of AML platforms; process design and optimisation; vendor selection; AI-driven risk detection; intelligent automation and workflow |
| **Training and insight** | Knowledge transfer and awareness | Board and management training; staff training; simulations and crisis exercises; webinars; reports and insights |

Standard line for the managed services block: "Our managed services support your daily operations in financial crime prevention, so that you can stay a step ahead of financial crime through proven expertise and prudence."

Standard line for the team: "We offer highly specialised expertise in financial crime prevention, gained from the financial sector and from supervisory authorities. Our combination of strategic and operational experience, with legal and technical capabilities, sets us apart." Use it only if it is in the profile's approved claims.

| Layer | Components |
|---|---|
| **Business-wide risk assessment** | The overarching layer. Sets what the rest must do. |
| **Governance and control** | Quality assurance; model validation; risk appetite; risk taxonomy; policy and instructions |
| **Customer lifecycle** | Onboarding; ongoing due diligence; offboarding |
| **FCP risk events** | Transaction monitoring; screening; fraud prevention; market manipulation; rogue trading. Flow: capture and transform → apply rules → alert → investigate → act → MI and SAR reporting. |
| **FCP intelligence** | Customer risk rating; AI and analytics; model risk management and maintenance |
| **Enablement foundation** | Technology; data; knowledge and training; change management; processes |
